title: Associate Commercial Counsel
location: San Francisco Bay Area or Remote (U.S.)
text:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Discord's Commercial & Marketing Legal (CoMa) team is the legal engine behind Discord's revenue and partnership business. We partner with Global Partnerships, Developer & Platform Solutions, Corporate Strategy, Ad Solutions, Data Science, AdTech, Marketing, and Procurement to structure and close the deals that bring games, creators, and brands to Discord's community. As Associate Commercial Counsel, you'll be a key advisor for integrating Discord's social features into games, enabling in-game commerce and digital collectibles, and building new monetization models alongside some of the biggest names in gaming and entertainment. You will also support our marketing and events teams on creative endeavors that promote Discord in the industry and to users. You'll handle a high volume of deals with real ownership, and you'll help shape how Discord approaches new partnership types at scale. This person will report to the Managing Counsel, Commercial & Marketing Legal.

What you'll be doing:

  • Draft, negotiate, and close a high volume of commercial agreements. These include Advertising, API and SDK integration agreements, commerce and in-app purchase agreements, and ad tech related transactions.
  • Negotiate IP licensing agreements with game, anime, and entertainment licensors for digital collectibles and in-app content.
  • Review, advise on, and support sponsorship and marketing efforts.
  • Structure novel monetization and revenue models, such as virtual currency, bundled subscriptions, rewards programs, and revenue share. 
  • Support payments and platform agreements, including payment processors, gift card distribution, and app store and developer program terms.
  • Build and maintain scalable templates, playbooks, and self-serve processes, including simplifying complex agreements into modular, easy-to-use forms.

What you should have:

  • A JD and active membership in good standing with at least one U.S. state bar. You also need to be eligible to register as in-house counsel in California.
  • At least 4 years of commercial transactional experience, with a combination of top law firm and/or in-house experience at a technology company preferred.
  • Experience drafting and negotiating complex commercial agreements, such as technology licensing, platform integrations, and revenue partnerships.
  • Experience with advertising, gaming, digital media, data privacy and consumer internet.
  • Understanding of privacy principles, especially with respect to commercial agreements involving the transfer or personal information.
  • Familiarity with marketing legal issues, including copyright, privacy, and consumer protection principles.
  • The ability to manage a high-volume docket while prioritizing effectively and meeting business timelines.
  • Sound business judgment and the ability to give practical, risk-calibrated advice in fast-moving, ambiguous situations.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex legal issues for non-lawyer stakeholders and run with work independently.

Bonus points:

  • Familiarity with payments, virtual currency, or subscription and bundling arrangements.
  • Experience with international or APAC counterparties.

text:

More broadly, Discord is about empowering people to find belonging in all kinds of communities, and those people trust us to keep their communications safe. Our Platform Security Engineering team protects the systems we use to create Discord, making the “secure way” the “easy way.”

We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a team of software engineers in articulating and pursuing the most leveraged opportunities to reduce security risk across Engineering. This team will design and build lovable “paved paths” for managing identities and access, shipping code, configuring cloud infrastructure, and operating services. If you’re an Engineering Manager who’s deeply curious, eager to own technically and socially complex projects, and excited to improve security and privacy at Discord, read on!

 

What you'll do

You’ll shape company-wide security strategy and lead a highly-autonomous and horizontally-integrated team of software engineers who will...

  • Develop and apply best-in-class secure baselines for cloud infrastructure, owning the security of all cloud environments
  • Manage infrastructure vulnerabilities while supporting a high-velocity engineering org with hundreds of developers
  • Secure first- and third-party software supply chains, from the dev environment through CI/CD and into production
  • Build and operate identity and access management (IAM) systems for humans and machines that are user-friendly and promote least privilege
  • Consult on risk assessments, architectural designs, threat models, code reviews, and more—pragmatically balancing security with other business considerations

What we look for

  • 3+ years of experience as people manager, having managed a team of 3+ security software engineers
  • Passion for creating diverse and inclusive teams and coaching engineers
  • 3+ years of experience securing systems with millions of users
  • Comfort with writing the roadmap, not just following one
  • Experience building in and securing cloud-based environments (we use GCP, Cloudflare, and AWS)
  • Expert reasoning about the security of complex systems, even if they contain unfamiliar components
  • Experience writing software in a general-purpose programming language (we use Python, Typescript, and Rust)
  • Experience developing with agentic AI, and a good grasp of AI security practices

Bonus points if you have…

  • Understanding of modern authentication and authorization concepts (e.g. RBAC, OAuth, Zero Trust network architectures, mTLS)

text:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Discord is opening an engineering hub in Lisbon, our first dedicated one outside of our San Francisco HQ. And we’re building it from the ground up. As a member of our founding team, you’ll help set the direction for teams across Core Technology, advancing work that keeps Discord reliable for millions of people around the world, helps our engineers move faster, and protects our platform at scale. You’ll also help shape the culture of the hub so it feels unmistakably Discord while developing a distinctly Lisbon identity of its own.

This is our first IT hire in EMEA, and it is a founding role. You will stand up and run the full employee technology surface across EMEA, based in our Lisbon office and supporting Discordians throughout the region. You are the trusted face of IT in the region and the coverage anchor for European hours, handling what cannot wait for San Francisco to wake up. This is a highly independent senior role for someone who navigates ambiguity, wears every hat, and turns a greenfield into a place that just works. You are measured by leverage and outcomes, not just tickets touched.

What you will do

  • Stand up IT for the region, starting with Lisbon: establish the office's physical technology footprint, build the local and regional vendor and ISP relationships, and set the day-to-day processes a growing EMEA presence needs, as the foundation the region's IT grows on.
  • Own the full surface end to end in region: identity and access, device and endpoint management, office network and connectivity, AV and meeting rooms, and SaaS, in partnership with Enterprise Security on the endpoint and identity surface.
  • Script and integrate across that surface: use vendor-native automation and APIs to connect those systems and write the glue that makes them work as one instead of a pile of consoles.
  • Run onboarding and offboarding for the region so a new Discordian is equipped on day one and deprovisioned on exit.
  • Be the EMEA coverage anchor: resolve what the timezone gap would otherwise stall, and keep async, well-documented handoffs with the team in San Francisco.
  • Look past the individual ticket to the workflow underneath: find the recurring breakdowns, automate them away, and measure the result in time and risk saved.
  • Participate in on-call rotations.

What you should have

  • Hands-on experience across most of the employee technology surface, with real depth in several areas and not all expected: identity (Okta), device management across both Mac (Jamf) and Windows (Intune), corporate networking (wireless, DNS/DHCP, VPN, Zero Trust access), SaaS and productivity (Google Workspace), collaboration and conferencing (Discord), and the meeting-room AV around it.
  • A track record of operating independently through ambiguity, ideally standing something up from scratch. You do not wait to be told what to fix.
  • Real automation chops: comfortable producing working scripts (Python is our go-to, and using AI to write them is fine), plus no-code and low-code workflows. You reach for automation before a runbook.
  • Excellent written communication and async discipline, since you will often be the only IT person in the room. Plus a business-problem mindset and a collaborative, low-ego, secure-by-design posture.
  • 8+ years of experience managing IT systems in high growth tech companies.

Bonus points

We're looking for a Marketing Program Manager to join our Partner Marketing team and help us execute co-marketing programs, events, and industry marketing with top game developers and technology partners. This role sits at the intersection of partnerships, marketing, and program management, and plays an important part in supporting partner relationships and program delivery across our platform.

Reporting to the Director, Partner Marketing, you'll work cross-functionally to help ensure the successful launch of win-win-win campaigns: good for players, good for partners, and good for our business. You'll help keep timelines, processes, and cross-functional coordination on track across sales, product, brand, creative, and channel teams.

 

What You'll Be Doing

Co-Marketing Execution

  • Support and execute partner co-marketing campaigns across channels including owned social, email, in-product placements, and live events.
  • Help maintain marketing "playbooks" and repeatable program templates that support consistency and faster time-to-launch across partners.
  • Support GTM planning for partner moments (new product launches, integrations, tentpole game releases), helping prepare materials and recommendations for review.
  • Coordinate with partners' marketing counterparts on creative direction, promotional timing, approvals, and campaign deliverables.

Cross-Functional Program Coordination

  • Provide day-to-day program support for Commerce partners, helping keep always-on promotions running smoothly.
  • Coordinate with Developer Solutions, Advertising, Commerce, PMM, and Channel Marketing teams to track timelines, deliverables, and responsibilities for partner-facing programs.
  • Maintain project timelines, flag dependencies and risks, and help facilitate regular syncs with internal stakeholders.
  • Maintain intake and request-tracking workflows (e.g., via Salesforce and Asana) so partner marketing requests are logged, prioritized, and actioned consistently.
  • Support the development of B2B marketing collateral and presentations in partnership with Product Marketing and Consumer Marketing teams (newsletters, blog posts, case study amplification).
  • Help coordinate partner workshops, innovation days, QBR presentations, and industry summits, using established frameworks and templates.

Reporting & Optimization

  • Track campaign performance against business KPIs — including revenue supported, daily account linked players (DALP), and Commerce GMV — and help synthesize insights for the team.
  • Help maintain a partner marketing roadmap that shows program activity and status for cross-functional visibility.
  • Flag recurring friction points (e.g., one-off approval requests, low-priority asks) to help the team improve processes over time.

 

What you should have

Experience

  • 5–6 years of experience in partner marketing, co-marketing, marketing operations, or program/project coordination — ideally in a tech, gaming, or platform company.
  • Experience supporting cross-functional marketing programs, from intake through launch and reporting.
  • Some experience working directly with external partners or clients in a marketing capacity.

Skills

text:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Discord is where the world's gamers hang out, and increasingly, it's the platform game developers build on. We're seeking a Senior Data Science Manager to lead Data Science for our Developer Platform: the SDKs, identity systems, and developer tools that connect games and their players to Discord.

What makes this role distinctive is the two-sided value equation at the heart of the platform. For game developers, we build tools that help studios grow player engagement and revenue, including data products that give them deeper insight into their players and communities. For players, we use signals from those same tools to make it easier to play and hang out with friends, deepen engagement across Discord, and deliver more relevant ads. 

Your team's job is to make both sides of that exchange demonstrably valuable. That means proving the platform's worth to developers with rigorous evidence, and ensuring the signals it generates create outsized, responsible value for Discord users.

If helping make Discord an even better place to hang out with your friends and communities sounds like an exciting challenge - we'd love to chat with you!

What you'll be doing

  • Manage, mentor, and develop a mission-driven team of Data Scientists embedded across the Developer Platform's core areas: identity, signals, and developer tools.
  • Own the vision and roadmap for data-driven decision-making across the Developer Platform org, and shape company strategy on how the platform creates value for both developers and Discord.
  • Strengthen the developer side of the value equation by shaping developer-facing data products, including metric definitions, benchmarking methodologies, and insight quality.

  • 3+ years managing and developing teams of Data Scientists, with a track record of growing ICs and raising the team's technical bar.

  • Proficiency in SQL and at least one data programming language (Python or R).

title: Senior Platform Security Engineer
text:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

More broadly, Discord is about empowering people to find belonging in all kinds of communities, and those people trust us to keep their communications safe. Our Platform Security Engineering team protects the systems we use to create Discord, making the "secure way" the "easy way."

We're looking for a Senior Engineer to advance this mission through security expertise, software development, and operational excellence, with a particular focus on identity and access management: who and what can access Discord's systems, how they authenticate, and how access stays scoped to what's actually needed. You'll help identify leveraged opportunities to reduce security risk across Engineering, then design and deliver technical solutions: lovable "paved paths" for managing identities and access, shipping code, configuring cloud infrastructure, and operating services.

If you're a security engineer with a deep interest in identity and access management, who's eager to own technically and socially complex projects, and excited to improve security and privacy at Discord, read on!

This position is based in our San Francisco office. For this role, the Hiring Manager would like folks to be in the office 1-2 days a week.

What you'll do

  • Own software engineering projects end-to-end on a highly autonomous, horizontally integrated team with a lot of leverage. This is a code-forward role!
  • Define what identity means for autonomous agents and other non-human actors at Discord (how they're provisioned, scoped, authenticated, authorized, and audited). As the role of these actors grows, and create primitives to implement that vision.
  • Build and evolve Access, Discord's employee authorization platform, to make permissions discoverable, role-based, least privilege, and self-serve; check out our blog post to learn more!
  • Design and harden our Zero Trust architecture, spanning human and service-to-service auth*n for Discord’s internal tooling.
  • Automate continuous permission right-sizing in the spirit of least privilege.
  • Develop and apply secure baselines for cloud identity, and help secure our software supply chain from the dev environment through CI/CD and into production.
  • Consult on risk assessments, architectural designs, threat models, code reviews, and more, pragmatically balancing security with other business considerations.

Example projects

  • Integrate service-to-service and agent-to-service authentication and authorization as out-of-the-box features in Discord's internal developer platform.
  • Build out service identity provisioning using PKI and mTLS, so services can authenticate each other without shared secrets.
  • Evaluate or extend infrastructure access tooling such as Teleport for short-lived, auditable access to hosts, databases, and internal systems.
  • Improve how secrets are issued, rotated, and scoped across our infrastructure.

What we look for

  • 5+ years of experience building and operating production systems or infrastructure
  • 3+ years of experience writing software in a general-purpose programming language (we mainly use Python, TypeScript, and Rust)
  • 3+ years of experience securing systems with millions of users
  • Experience building or operating identity and access management systems: authentication, authorization, or access control at scale
  • Understanding of modern authentication and authorization concepts (e.g. RBAC, OAuth, OIDC, SSO, Zero Trust network architectures, mTLS, cloud IAM)
  • Experience building in and securing multi-cloud environments (e.g. GCP, Cloudflare, AWS)
  • Experience designing and building software for customers (internal or external) beyond your immediate team

Bonus points if you have…

  • Experience defining and orchestrating containers (e.g. via Kubernetes, Docker, Distroless, OCI)
  • Familiarity with build and CI/CD technologies (e.g. Terraform, Bazel, Buildkite)
  • Provisioned or managed service and workload identity using PKI, including issuing and operating mTLS between services
  • Experience with Zero Trust platforms such as Cloudflare Access and Teleport, for auditable access to apps, hosts, and internal systems
  • Experience with secrets management systems (e.g. Vault, or a cloud KMS or secrets manager), including rotation and least-privilege access to secrets
  • Developed and debugged distributed systems atop GCP, Cloudflare, and/or AWS
  • Led complex migrations or risk management programs across an engineering organization
  • Built or operated a service mesh (e.g. Envoy, Istio)
  • Managed and secured VMs or bare-metal hosts (e.g. Linux, Salt)
  • Practices to discover industry tools and knowledge that can multiply your team's impact

You will not be maintaining a status quo or joining an existing backlog: you will define the discipline, set the technical foundation, and build the platform that lets the internal systems enabling Discordians scale with the company.

Discord's mission is to cultivate belonging, and doing that at scale requires internal systems that move as fast as the product itself. The mission of this role is to turn our enterprise infrastructure into self-service software. Your job is to replace manual consoles and tickets with a platform of reusable primitives, building blocks like "provision a device" or "push an IAM policy or app integration through code," exposed through clean APIs and self-service portals. As a code-forward Staff engineer, you will design abstractions that hide the messy reality of Okta, Jamf, and Terraform (our identity, device management, and infrastructure-as-code tools) behind interfaces people actually want to use, operating with a platform-as-a-product mindset.

What You'll Do

  • Manage the device fleet as code: Move device configuration off consoles and into versioned, API-driven infrastructure for endpoint management and hardware provisioning.
  • Automate the identity layer: Manage identity systems and their connections to downstream apps as code, from SSO and SCIM integrations to account workflows, so changes ship through version control and CI/CD instead of an admin console.
  • Own app delivery and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC): Build deployment pipelines and provisioning patterns that let internal systems be built and changed safely, establishing CI/CD standards.
  • Build the self-service layer: Design and ship the APIs, CLIs, and portals that compose primitives into paved paths, like a new hire's first day, where software access and group memberships land in one automated, auditable flow.
  • Set the foundation: Define the technical direction and architecture for the discipline, writing the RFCs and documentation that future hires will build on.

What You Should Have

  • 6+ years building and operating production software and systems at a technology company, with a track record of owning ambiguous projects end to end.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals. You write production code (we lean on Python, TypeScript and Rust), and design, test, and ship it. This is not a systems admin role.
  • Deep, hands-on IAM experience (SSO, SCIM, OAuth/OIDC, RBAC) and fluency with infrastructure as code (Terraform) and CI/CD.
  • Experience treating endpoint and fleet management as an API-driven engineering surface at scale.
  • A platform-as-a-product mindset. You have built self-service tooling that people chose to adopt.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and a founder's temperament; energized by building from scratch.

Bonus Points

  • Hands-on experience with Okta, Jamf, or Intune.
  • Experience with identity and access governance for non-human, workload, or AI-agent principals.

title: Threat Investigator Team Lead
text:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Discord’s mission is to give people the power to create space to find belonging in their lives. Every day, millions of people trust Discord to be a place where they can talk, spend time together, and build community. Keeping that space safe starts with teams like ours.

Discord’s Violent Actors Team, part of the broader Threat Operations organization within Trust & Safety, identifies and disrupts violent and extremist actors and networks. As Threat Investigations Team Lead, you will manage and develop a team of investigators and analysts responsible for detecting, investigating, and disrupting ongoing and emerging threats.

You will be a player-coach: setting a high bar for investigative quality while staying close enough to the work to guide complex cases and incident response. You will help early-career investigators build their tradecraft, turn investigative findings into actionable intelligence, and collaborate with internal and external partners during high-risk incidents. You will report to the team’s Senior Manager.

This position is US-based and can be remote but if you live in the Bay Area, you're welcome to work from our beautiful SF office. #LI-Remote

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Manage, coach, and develop a small team of investigators and analysts, setting clear expectations and providing timely, actionable feedback.
  • Own the team’s investigative quality, workload prioritization, queue health, and performance.
  • Serve as the first point of escalation for complex, ambiguous, or high-risk investigations, helping the team make sound and well-documented decisions.
  • Act as a player-coach: guide deep-dive network investigations, build the team’s tradecraft across case development, network analysis, proactive detection, and intelligence production, and help the team identify new detection and disruption opportunities.
  • Translate investigative signals and subject-matter expertise into recommendations about threat prioritization, policy gaps, and enforcement interventions.
  • Coordinate with law enforcement, government, industry, and other external partners when investigations or incidents require external engagement.
  • Support hiring, onboarding, performance management, and career development while fostering an inclusive, resilient, and sustainable team culture.

What You Should Have

  • 5+ years of experience in threat intelligence, investigations, incident response, or a related field, with at least 2 years of prior people-management experience.
  • Deep expertise in at least one extremist or violent-threat-actor ecosystem, with the analytical flexibility to develop proficiency across new harm areas as priorities evolve.
  • Demonstrated ability to coach investigators, raise quality standards, deliver constructive feedback, and support the growth of people at different stages of their careers.
  • Strong judgment in ambiguous, fast-changing situations — including defining scope, proposing solutions, and driving work to completion with limited oversight — while balancing immediate harm reduction against policy, legal, operational, and company-risk considerations.
  • Fluency with investigative and case-management tooling, and the ability to use data and detection signals to guide team priorities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex and sensitive subjects for non-expert audiences.
  • A collaborative approach to cross-functional work, with the ability to build consensus and coordinate across teams, disciplines, and time zones.

Bonus Points

  • Experience supporting teams that regularly work with sensitive or potentially disturbing material.
  • Additional language proficiency, particularly in languages relevant to high-harm threat-actor communities.

title: Customer Success Manager — Japan
text:
Role Description

As a Customer Success Manager at Dropbox, you will own the post-sale customer strategy and relationship for a portfolio of customers. You will help customers realize measurable value from their investment while driving product adoption, retention, growth, and Net Revenue Retention (NRR).

You will serve as a trusted advisor throughout the customer journey, developing a deep understanding of each customer’s business priorities, technical environment, key stakeholders, and evolving needs. Using customer insights, product adoption signals, stakeholder relationships, and demonstrated business value, you will proactively set priorities, address risks, and identify opportunities to strengthen the customer’s long-term partnership with Dropbox.
 
You will develop strong technical fluency across the Dropbox platform and engage confidently with IT administrators on product capabilities, security, configuration, integrations, governance, and customer workflows. You will help translate customers’ business and technical requirements into practical use cases, recommendations, and actionable insights for internal teams.
You will partner closely with Sales and cross-functional teams to align on account strategy, navigate technical and commercial complexities, mitigate renewal risks, identify appropriate growth opportunities, and deliver successful customer outcomes.
 
The successful candidate is results-driven, commercially minded, technically savvy, and customer-focused. They are comfortable navigating complex customer organizations, taking ownership of customer strategy, and influencing both technical and business stakeholders. They bring strong Customer Success experience and a demonstrated ability to drive adoption, manage risk, support successful renewals, and deliver measurable retention and growth outcomes in a B2B SaaS environment.

Responsibilities

  • Build strong relationships across customer organizations, serving as a trusted advisor to executive sponsors, business leaders, technical administrators, and other key stakeholders.
  • Take ownership of the customer strategy across an assigned portfolio, setting priorities and proactively driving adoption, value realization, stakeholder engagement, retention, and growth.
  • Develop strong technical fluency across the Dropbox platform and confidently engage with IT administrators on questions involving product capabilities, security, configuration, integrations, governance, and customer workflows.
  • Understand customers’ technical environments and business requirements, helping translate them into practical use cases, recommendations, and actionable feedback for internal teams.
  • Lead strategic customer engagements—including product education, use-case development, Success Business Reviews, and value-based renewal discussions—that connect Dropbox capabilities to business outcomes.
  • Partner closely with Sales and cross-functional teams to develop account strategies, remove technical and commercial blockers, mitigate renewal risks, and identify appropriate expansion opportunities.
  • Use customer feedback, product usage, business context, and stakeholder engagement to prioritize actions, represent the voice of the customer, and contribute to repeatable playbooks and best practices.

Requirements

  • 4+ years of experience in B2B SaaS Customer Success, Account Management, Solutions Consulting, Professional Services, or a comparable customer-facing role, with experience driving product adoption and business value, managing ongoing customer relationships, and engaging technical stakeholders.
  • Business and commercial acumen, with a willingness to develop the skills needed to own assigned customer renewals from 2027, including early renewal planning, commercial discussions, and coordination with Sales and relevant teams to support retention and identify appropriate growth opportunities.
  • Technical aptitude and product curiosity, with the ability to learn SaaS products, customer environments, configurations, and workflows. Comfortable engaging with IT administrators, investigating unfamiliar technical questions, and translating product capabilities into practical guidance.
  • Ability to build relationships across customer organizations, from technical administrators to executive stakeholders, and manage a portfolio across Japan and Korea. The initial allocation is expected to be approximately 80% Japan and 20% Korea, with flexibility to adjust based on business and customer needs.
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to use customer insights, usage data, and business context to assess customer health, identify renewal risks, prioritize actions, and recommend practical solutions.
  • A proactive self-starter who can ramp up quickly, seek out information, navigate ambiguity, and take ownership of moving customer plans forward without close day-to-day direction. Able to build effective working relationships and collaborate with Sales, Product, Support, Legal, Finance, and other teams.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • Fluent spoken and written Japanese, including business communication.
  • Business-level Korean and English.
  • Ability to engage customers in Japanese and Korean and collaborate with global teams in English.
  • Willingness to travel for customer visits in Japan and Korea, and internationally for company offsites and sales kickoffs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience owning or contributing to customer renewals and retention, with examples of identifying risk, coordinating mitigation plans, demonstrating customer value, and supporting successful renewal outcomes.
  • Experience managing strategic customer relationships with multiple stakeholders, complex decision-making processes, and changing business priorities, ideally in Japan or Korea.

title: Integrated Campaign Strategist
text:
Role Description

Dropbox is hiring an Integrated Campaign Strategist to architect and orchestrate marketing campaigns for priority product launches and evergreen marketing motions. This role turns business priorities, audience insight, and product positioning into a clear campaign strategy that defines the audience, narrative, journey, channel roles, activation sequence, and measurement plan.

You will be the steward of how these campaigns show up in market across owned, earned, and paid channels. Working across Product Marketing, Brand and Creative, Comms, Web, Lifecycle, Paid Media, Content, Events, Marketing Operations, Analytics, and Sales, you will align teams around one integrated plan, connect individual activations into a coherent enterprise buyer experience, and guide the campaign from brief through launch, optimization, and learning.

This is a senior individual contributor role for a strategist who can lead through influence, make tradeoffs in ambiguity, and balance strong market storytelling with measurable business impact. You will help Dropbox bring important product stories to enterprise audiences with greater consistency, relevance, and effectiveness.

Responsibilities

  • Campaign strategy architecture: Translate mid-market and enterprise business goals, product positioning, audience insight, and market context into integrated campaign strategies for key launches and evergreen motions, including objectives, audience, narrative, journey, channel roles, phasing, and measurement.
  • Cross channel orchestration: Build and manage the integrated activation plan across owned, earned, and paid channels so that web, lifecycle, content, social, communications, events, partner, and media programs work as one connected campaign rather than separate channel plans.
  • In-market stewardship: Own the campaign through launch and sustainment, protecting the strategic throughline while ensuring creative, messaging, timing, and audience experience remain coherent across touchpoints and regions.
  • Cross-functional leadership: Establish the brief, operating rhythm, decision rights, milestones, dependencies, and readiness criteria that align Product Marketing, Brand and Creative, Communications, channel owners, Marketing Operations, Marketing Data Science, regional partners, and Sales.
  • Audience and journey design: Define target audiences and buying groups, map the role of each touchpoint across the customer journey, and ensure campaign experiences respond to buyer needs, market moments, and stages of consideration.
  • Performance and optimization: Partner with Marketing Data Science and channel owners to define full funnel success measures, synthesize owned, earned, and paid signals, identify what is driving or limiting performance, and recommend changes to audience, narrative, creative, sequencing, or channel mix.
  • Portfolio learning and scale: Capture campaign insights, codify reusable plays, distinguish enduring strategy from launch specific execution, and apply learning across the enterprise campaign portfolio to improve future launches and evergreen motions.

Requirements

  • 8+ years B2B marketing experience in integrated campaigns, enterprise marketing, product marketing activation, brand to demand, or a related discipline, ideally in SaaS or technology.
  • Direct experience building out campaign strategy and accountable to the outcome (pipeline generation, revenue generation).
  • Demonstrated ownership of complex integrated campaigns from strategy and brief through activation, optimization, and post campaign learning.
  • Strong campaign architecture skills, including audience definition, narrative development, buyer journey design, channel planning, phasing, and measurement.
  • Experience orchestrating owned, earned, and paid programs and understanding the distinct role each plays in building awareness, consideration, demand, and customer growth.
  • Ability to translate product positioning and enterprise customer insight into a cohesive market story and connected audience experience across multiple teams and touchpoints.
  • Strong cross functional leadership and program judgment, including the ability to establish decision rights, navigate competing priorities, resolve dependencies, and influence without direct authority.
  • Analytical fluency and experience using campaign, brand, engagement, and revenue signals to evaluate performance, communicate impact, and make optimization decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading enterprise product launch campaigns and building evergreen motions for a multi product B2B portfolio.
  • Experience partnering closely with Corporate Communications, analyst relations, customer advocacy, or social teams to connect earned programs with owned and paid activation.
  • Experience marketing to complex enterprise buying groups across industries, company sizes, regions, or stages of maturity.
  • Familiarity with marketing automation, CRM, media, intent, experimentation, and attribution platforms used to activate and measure integrated campaigns.
  • Experience using AI to accelerate research, briefing, content variation, synthesis, or analysis while retaining human ownership of strategy, judgment, and brand decisions.

Durable Skills

AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technology continue to evolve:

  • Awareness: Understand yourself and others.
  • Judgment: Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations.
  • Adaptability: Learn, adjust, and stay effective through change.
  • Connection: Communicate, collaborate, and build trust.

To learn more about why these skills matter and what the data shows about thriving through change, read this blog post from our Chief People Officer, Melanie Rosenwasser.

title: Principal Software Engineer, Product Engineering
text:
Role Description

As a Principal Engineer at Dropbox, you will own company critical, loosely defined technical problems with multi year impact, operating at the intersection of technology, product, business strategy, and applied AI. You will define long term technical direction for customer facing experiences used by millions, identifying where AI meaningfully improves customer value and translating evolving business context and industry advances into durable, multi area strategies and roadmaps that shape how Dropbox builds, scales, and innovates, while remaining hands on in software development where it provides the greatest leverage.
 
Your influence will span organizations, setting foundational architecture, driving execution standards, and aligning senior technical and product leaders across boundaries. You will lead the responsible introduction and adoption of AI across product capabilities and engineering workflows, bring clarity to the most complex decisions, institutionalize engineering excellence, and contribute directly through critical design, prototyping, and code reviews.
 
In return, you will operate as a trusted technical partner to senior leadership, shape systems and platforms including AI powered foundations that define Dropbox’s future, and act as a company level technical strategist, advancing Dropbox’s mission to create a more enlightened way of working.

Responsibilities

  • Own and drive technical outcomes across multiple teams and organizations, delivering company critical customer and business impact at scale.
  • Define long term technical strategy and partner with senior Product and Engineering leaders as the technical owner for the most important company objectives.
  • Tackle the most ambiguous and far reaching technical and product problems, shaping what the company builds as much as how it builds it.
  • Remain deeply hands on in software development, owning and implementing the most critical, complex, and foundational parts of the system where leverage is highest.
  • Influence and align roadmaps across organizations, resolving structural bottlenecks and changing how Dropbox builds and operates.
  • Architect and evolve foundational systems (this may involve both frontend and backend systems) and platforms that enable new product capabilities and operate reliably at the scale of hundreds of millions of users.
  • Model exceptional technical judgment and execution rigor, setting and sustaining high engineering standards across a distributed, virtual environment
  • Drive AI adoption both to increase productivity and to produce AI based features.

Requirements

  • Advanced degree in Computer Science or a related technical field involving substantial software development, or equivalent industry experience demonstrating deep technical mastery.
  • 15+ years of experience designing, building, and evolving large scale software systems with sustained impact across multiple teams or organizations.
  • Demonstrated success operating at a Principal level, owning company critical technical problems and influencing long term technical direction.
  • Strong experience building consumer facing products at scale, with a deep understanding of user experience, performance, reliability, and operational excellence.
  • Broad and deep technical expertise across multiple domains, including several of frontend, mobile, search, databases, storage systems, concurrency, and distributed systems.
  • Practical experience applying modern ML, LLM based APIs, and agentic frameworks in production systems, with sound judgment around quality, cost, and risk.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and persuasively to senior engineering, product, and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience defining and scaling company wide platforms or architectural standards that are adopted across multiple organizations.
  • Proven track record of leading the introduction of new technologies such as AI or ML into core products or engineering workflows with durable impact.
  • Experience operating in highly distributed, virtual first engineering organizations at global scale.

title: Program Manager, Customer Programs
text:
Role Description

Dropbox is looking for a Senior Program Manager, Customer Programs to lead complex, cross-functional programs that deepen how we engage, learn from, and deliver value to our customers.

This role sits at the intersection of customers, GTM, and Product. You will lead programs that bring customers into important moments across the product and customer lifecycle - from early product learning and customer validation to launches, adoption, advocacy, and strategic customer engagement. You’ll ensure we are engaging the right customers for the right purpose, creating a coordinated experience across Dropbox, and turning what we learn into clear actions for the business.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with significant autonomy and executive visibility. You’ll take high-priority initiatives that often span multiple functions, have evolving requirements, or lack an established operating model and turn them into well-run programs. You’ll define the objective, determine the right program approach, align stakeholders, establish ownership and decision points, manage dependencies and risks, and drive execution through measurable outcomes.

A critical part of the role is representing the customer experience across the entire program, not simply coordinating internal teams. You’ll think deliberately about who we engage, why we are engaging them, what we are asking of them, how Dropbox shows up across touchpoints, and how we close the loop on their participation. The customer should experience one coordinated Dropbox program even when many internal teams are involved behind the scenes.

You’ll work across Sales, Customer Success, Product, Research, Design, Engineering, Product Marketing, Customer Marketing, Analytics, and other teams depending on the program. Over time, you’ll also help Dropbox build more repeatable ways to run customer programs - creating playbooks and operating mechanisms that allow successful approaches to scale without creating unnecessary process.

Responsibilities

  • Lead complex customer programs end-to-end, translating ambiguous business priorities into clear objectives, operating plans, milestones, decision points, owners, risks, and measurable outcomes.
  • Create a coordinated customer experience across Dropbox by partnering with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and other teams to ensure customers receive clear expectations, thoughtful engagement, and appropriate follow-through.
  • Lead large cross-functional teams through competing priorities, dependencies, and ambiguity, driving decisions and accountability without relying on formal authority.
  • Connect customer signal to action by ensuring feedback, behavior, and program results reach the right Product and GTM owners and translate into decisions, changes, or clearly documented next steps.
  • Build practical and scalable program infrastructure - including workbacks, decision rights, readiness criteria, status mechanisms, risk/escalation paths, measurement, and reusable playbooks - while avoiding unnecessary process.
  • Provide clear executive-level synthesis of program health, customer signal, risks, tradeoffs, decisions, and recommendations.

Requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in program management, customer programs, strategy & operations, GTM operations, product operations, or a related field, with demonstrated ownership of complex cross-functional programs.
  • Demonstrated ability to take a highly ambiguous initiative from problem definition through execution, measurement, and outcome, operating independently with limited direction.
  • Experience leading programs involving customers or customer-facing teams, with strong judgment around customer selection, engagement, communications, expectations, and experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple senior stakeholders and functions with different priorities, dependencies, and decision rights while maintaining momentum and accountability.
  • Strong operating judgment: able to determine the appropriate level of structure for a problem, make tradeoffs, simplify where possible, and build repeatable mechanisms where needed.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex qualitative and quantitative information into concise recommendations, decisions, and executive updates.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate as a hands-on senior IC, moving comfortably between strategic problem-solving and the detailed execution required to deliver a program successfully.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading customer programs involving early product feedback, beta/early-access programs, customer validation, product launches, adoption, advocacy, or strategic customer engagement.
  • Experience working across both Product/EPD and GTM organizations and translating customer needs and business requirements between the two.
  • Experience building a new program or operating model and scaling it across products, customer segments, or business priorities.
  • Experience in B2B SaaS, enterprise software, collaboration/productivity technology, or another complex technology environment.
  • Experience using AI and automation to improve program execution, customer insights, synthesis, reporting, or operating efficiency.

Durable Skills

  • Awareness: Understand yourself and others.
  • Judgment: Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations.
  • Adaptability: Learn, adjust, and stay effective through change.
  • Connection: Communicate, collaborate, and build trust.

title: Senior Corporate Enterprise Platform Engineer, Windows
text:
Role Description

As a Senior Client Platform Engineer on CorpFleet Engineering, you will own and improve Dropbox’s Windows endpoint platform. You will bring deep Windows and Intune expertise, make patching and application delivery more reliable, and build automation that reduces recurring work for the team.

This is a hands-on role combining Windows technical ownership with the development of a more code-managed endpoint platform. You will help evaluate and adopt FleetDM, osquery, infrastructure-as-code, and GitOps practices where they improve reliability, visibility, and maintainability. You will strengthen the current environment while building and validating the path forward—not assume that replacing a tool is the answer.

You will work with CorpInfra, IAM, Security, and support teams to make practical technical decisions, lead multi-phase improvements, and clarify ownership. You will also mentor teammates through pairing, code review, and shared operational practices. This is an individual-contributor role, not a people-management position.

Responsibilities

  • Own endpoint reliability and lifecycle management. Improve provisioning, application delivery, updates, security configuration, and troubleshooting across the endpoint environment.
  • Make patching predictable and safe. Strengthen update workflows through testing, controlled rollouts, and remediation.
  • Make fleet health trustworthy and actionable. Improve reporting on device health, patching, and configuration, with clear ownership for resolving issues.
  • Build maintainable automation. Turn recurring work into reliable, tested workflows that other engineers can operate.
  • Advance code-managed endpoint operations. Adopt tools and practices that improve configuration management, validation, and deployment.
  • Lead cross-functional platform improvements. Define practical roadmaps, resolve dependencies, and balance security, reliability, employee experience, and team capacity.
  • Strengthen the team’s capability. Mentor teammates, review code and designs, and document reusable practices that improve coverage across the endpoint team.

Requirements

  • Significant experience engineering and operating Windows endpoint environments, with personal ownership beyond ticket handling or routine console administration.
  • Deep hands-on Intune experience across device lifecycle, configuration and compliance policies, application management, update workflows, and relevant Entra ID dependencies.
  • Strong Windows troubleshooting skills across operating-system behavior, services, logs, networking, certificates, identity, and security controls. Able to distinguish reported management status from actual endpoint health.
  • Recent ownership of Windows and third-party application patching, including staged deployment, user-impact validation, failed-device handling, exceptions, and recovery.
  • Strong practical PowerShell skills and familiarity with at least one additional programming language, such as Python, Go, or C#. Experience building and maintaining production automation or systems integrations.
  • Demonstrated use of version control, code review, automated checks, and controlled deployment for operational changes. Able to explain safe retries, failure handling, secrets management, and configuration drift.
  • Ability to independently define and deliver multi-phase work, prioritize under ambiguity, partner across teams, and mentor other engineers.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including concise technical decisions, incident updates, runbooks, and effective asynchronous collaboration.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Production experience with FleetDM on Windows, including agent operations, policies, queries, targeting, API integrations, or configuration managed through GitOps.
  • Practical osquery and SQL experience for endpoint inventory, health, or security use cases, including query validation, performance considerations, and handling stale or missing results.
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code or declarative configuration, continuous integration and delivery, and migration or coexistence between endpoint-management platforms.
  • Experience with Automox, Patch My PC, or comparable tools, and with endpoint privilege management, application control, encryption, or other security controls.
  • Experience supporting developer-heavy, distributed environments and contributing reusable automation across Windows, macOS, or Linux.

text:
Role Description

We are seeking a Senior FP&A Partner to help shape and accelerate growth across our core business. This highly visible role will serve as a strategic thought partner to Product leadership, using financial analysis, business insights, and structured problem-solving to influence both near-term priorities and long-term strategy.

The ideal candidate combines strong financial acumen with a deep understanding of SaaS business models and growth drivers. They will translate complex data into clear insights, identify opportunities to improve business performance, and help leaders evaluate investments and strategic tradeoffs. Success in this role requires a self-starter who is comfortable navigating ambiguity, building structure where it does not yet exist, and collaborating across Product, Finance, Data Science, Marketing, and other cross-functional teams.

This individual will also be expected to embrace AI-enabled ways of working, using modern tools to improve the speed, quality, and scalability of financial analysis and decision support.

  • Build driver-based financial models that connect product performance and customer behavior to revenue, ARR, retention, and profitability

  • Develop business cases and scenario analyses that clearly articulate expected returns, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs
  • Partner across Product, Finance, Data Science, and Marketing to establish targets, define success metrics, and evaluate business performance
  • Identify emerging trends, performance gaps, and growth opportunities, translating complex data into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership

title: Senior Manager, APJ Field & Channel Marketing
text:
Role Description

As Senior Manager, APJ Field & Channel Marketing, you will lead the development and execution of Dropbox’s regional marketing strategy across the entire Asia-Pacific and Japan region. You will bring the greatest depth of focus to Dropbox’s Tier 1 markets—Australia/New Zealand, Singapore, Korea, India, and Japan—while building fit-for-market programs for Tier 2 markets including Vietnam, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. Reporting to the Chief Marketing Officer, you will work in close partnership with the Regional VP of Sales to translate business priorities into integrated marketing strategies and campaigns that create pipeline, accelerate opportunities, and support regional sales growth.

This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role at the intersection of field marketing, channel marketing, sales, and Dropbox’s global marketing organization. Field and channel marketing will be equally important as Dropbox evolves toward a hybrid go-to-market model in ANZ and adapts its approach across APJ. You will build the regional marketing plan, manage the regional budget, and measure performance against clear business outcomes. You will also manage and develop our Japan Marketing team, ensuring our regional approach combines consistent strategy and operating discipline with strong local-market relevance.
 
You will be Dropbox Marketing’s senior voice in the region—bringing APJ customer, partner, and market insights into global planning while adapting global campaigns for local audiences. The ideal candidate is a collaborative, commercially minded leader who can move comfortably between executive-level strategy, people leadership, and hands-on campaign execution.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and own the integrated field and channel marketing strategy for APJ, aligned with regional sales priorities and Dropbox’s global marketing strategy.
  • Partner closely with the Regional VP of Sales and sales leadership to develop regional and country-level plans that create qualified pipeline, accelerate priority opportunities, and support revenue growth.
  • Lead the planning and execution of regional marketing programs across field events, executive experiences, account-based initiatives, integrated campaigns, partner and channel activations, webinars, and other locally relevant tactics.
  • Build an equally strong field and channel marketing motion, balancing direct-to-customer and partner-led investments by market using customer insight, sales priorities, partner opportunity, and performance data.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the Japan Marketing team by establishing clear goals, operating rhythms, and opportunities for growth while enabling strong local execution.
  • Build strong relationships with regional sales, partner sales, and channel leaders; create joint plans with priority partners and develop co-marketing programs that extend Dropbox’s market reach and generate partner-sourced or partner-influenced demand.
  • Translate global campaigns, positioning, and content into regionally relevant programs, partnering with global Campaigns, Product Marketing, Brand, Digital, Communications, Marketing Operations, and other teams.
  • Own the regional marketing budget, agency and vendor relationships, program calendar, forecasting, and performance reporting; continuously optimize investments based on pipeline impact and ROI.
  • Establish clear KPIs and operating cadences with Sales and Marketing Operations, including regular planning sessions and business reviews that connect marketing activity to pipeline creation and opportunity progression.
  • Represent APJ within the global marketing organization, sharing market intelligence, customer and partner feedback, competitive insight, and regional best practices to improve company-wide strategy and execution.
  • Build a scalable regional marketing playbook that balances consistency across APJ with the distinct needs, cultures, routes to market, and buying behaviors of individual countries.
  • Travel within the region and internationally as needed to support team leadership, sales planning, partner engagement, and key programs—approximately 20%

Requirements

  • 10+ years of progressive B2B marketing experience, including significant experience in regional, field, demand generation, and/or channel marketing within enterprise software, SaaS, or another technology environment.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing multi-country APJ marketing strategies that produced measurable pipeline and sales impact.
  • People-management experience, including coaching and developing marketers working across different countries, cultures, or time zones.
  • Proven ability to operate as a strategic partner to senior sales leaders, translate sales priorities into marketing plans, and build alignment through planning and business reviews.
  • Experience leading an integrated mix of field and channel programs, including events, account-based programs, partner co-marketing, campaigns, and pipeline-acceleration initiatives.

title: Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing
text:
Role Description

As the Senior Manager of Lifecycle Marketing, you will own Dropbox’s lifecycle marketing strategy across onboarding, engagement, retention, monetization, expansion, cross-sell, and re-engagement. You will lead a team of lifecycle marketers and build a portfolio of programs that help customers discover value, expand their use of Dropbox, and deepen their relationship with our products over time.

This is a senior people leadership role with direct accountability for business outcomes. You will set the lifecycle strategy and roadmap, determine where the team should invest, establish how programs are prioritized and measured, and stay close enough to the work to raise the quality of execution and unblock the highest-priority initiatives.

You will work closely with Product Growth, Product, Product Marketing, Data Science, Marketing Operations, and other marketing teams. Lifecycle Marketing will own customer communication strategy, channel planning, lifecycle program design, and marketing execution.

The opportunity is broader than running an email program. Dropbox has a large global customer base, multiple products, and both product-led and sales-assisted customer motions. The Head of Lifecycle Marketing will define how those pieces connect across the customer lifecycle and build the operating model needed to move from individual campaigns toward scalable growth programs.

Responsibilities

  • Own Dropbox’s lifecycle marketing strategy and roadmap across onboarding, engagement, retention, monetization, expansion, and multi-product adoption.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of lifecycle marketers, with clear goals, operating rhythms, and accountability for business outcomes.
  • Build and manage a portfolio of lifecycle programs using customer behavior, product usage, segmentation, triggers, and personalization to improve adoption, retention, and revenue.
  • Partner with Product Growth, Product Marketing, Data Science, Marketing Operations, and other cross-functional teams to connect lifecycle communications with activation, in-product discovery, monetization, and expansion while maintaining clear ownership across teams.
  • Establish a strong experimentation and measurement approach, using controlled tests, holdouts, cohort analysis, customer behavior, and revenue to determine what creates incremental impact.
  • Build the operating model for lifecycle marketing, including prioritization, planning, governance, and the technical and data capabilities required to execute reliably at scale.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of experience across lifecycle marketing, CRM, retention, growth marketing, customer engagement, or closely related disciplines, ideally in a SaaS, subscription, or product-led business.

  • Demonstrated experience setting lifecycle strategy and translating it into programs that improve customer adoption, retention, monetization, expansion, or revenue.
  • Deep experience with customer segmentation, behavioral triggers, personalization, experimentation, and marketing automation.
  • Strong technical fluency across CRM and lifecycle systems, customer data, campaign orchestration, measurement, deliverability, and related operational requirements.
  • Strong business judgment and experience working across Product, Product Growth, Data Science, Marketing Operations, Engineering, and Product Marketing to turn complex inputs into clear priorities and decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading lifecycle marketing in a product-led growth business with both self-serve and sales-assisted motions.

title: Senior Program Manager,  Employee Experience
text:
Role Description

Dropbox’s Virtual First team researches, tests, and scales better ways of working for a distributed organization. We combine organizational research, experimentation, behavioral science, technology, and employee experience to continuously improve how Dropboxers work—wherever they are.

As a Senior Program Manager, Employee Experience, you will own a strategic Virtual First work stream focused on tool optimization and technology-enabled ways of working, identifying opportunities to improve employee effectiveness and translating those opportunities into research, experiments, recommendations, and scalable organizational change.

This role combines program management with research, innovation, and cross-functional stakeholder management. You will manage a portfolio of interconnected programs rather than a single project, with particular focus on knowledge management, AI enablement, and building employee confidence with tools and technology. You will establish research priorities, design and facilitate experiments, synthesize findings, and work with partners across Dropbox to turn evidence into better ways of working.

Success in this role means creating new knowledge, translating that knowledge into clear recommendations, and driving measurable improvements in employee effectiveness, tool confidence, and adoption of AI-enabled and technology-supported ways of working.

Responsibilities

  • Own the strategy, roadmap, priorities, and outcomes of a Virtual First work stream focused on technology, including tools, workflows, automations, AI enablement, and knowledge management
  • Design and lead organizational research, pilots, and experiments that test new ways of working
  • Translate qualitative and quantitative findings into actionable recommendations, behavioral frameworks, and operating models for downstream adoption
  • Manage a portfolio of concurrent programs and initiatives from initial scoping through research, validation, and enablement planning
  • Establish clear objectives, success measures, milestones, risks, and reporting across the work stream
  • Facilitate cross-functional Steering Committees and initiatives involving stakeholders across People, Technology, Communications, Operations, and other business functions
  • Partner with People Analytics and other measurement experts to establish research methodologies and evaluate outcomes.

Requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in program management, organizational effectiveness, workplace strategy, employee experience, innovation, research, or a related discipline. 
  • Expertise in tools and technology enablement, including AI adoption, knowledge management, digital workflows, automation, and the design of technology-enabled ways of working that improve employee effectiveness.
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading complex, cross-functional programs from ambiguity through measurable outcomes.
  • Experience designing and managing research, pilots, experiments, or other evidence-based innovation programs.
  • Strong understanding of Virtual First, distributed, hybrid, or modern ways of working.
  • Excellent written, verbal, facilitation, and executive communication skills.
  • Comfort working in ambiguity and proactively identifying opportunities rather than waiting for assignments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a distributed or Virtual First organization.

title: Senior Technical Solutions Specialist
text:
Role Description

The Dropbox Sales and Channel team helps organisations transform how they work through technology. We partner with customers to understand their business challenges and develop solutions that deliver practical, measurable value.

As a Solutions Consultant, you’ll combine technical depth with commercial judgement to help customers evaluate and adopt Dropbox products. With our work on DBX Platform, this role places particular emphasis on hands-on API experience, integrations and technical solution design.

You’ll work directly with customer technical teams to understand their environments, design connected workflows and validate solutions through demonstrations, pilots and proofs of concept. You’ll bring experience working with APIs and scripting languages, alongside the ability to explain technical decisions and business value to stakeholders ranging from developers and IT teams to senior executives.

Working across Direct Sales and Channel, you’ll support the full sales cycle—from discovery and technical validation through to deployment planning and handover. You’ll help shape customer solutions, influence product development through customer feedback and deepen your expertise across Dropbox’s products and platform capabilities.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with Direct Sales and Channel teams to translate customer business and technical requirements into secure, practical solutions using Dropbox products, add-ons and third-party integrations.
  • Lead technical discovery, demonstrations, pilots and proofs of concept, working directly with customer technical teams to establish success criteria, test feasibility and resolve technical challenges.
  • Design, build and validate API-based integrations and tailored workflows that address customer requirements and demonstrate the value of Dropbox products including DBX Platform.
  • Deliver technical enablement and training to Sales Representatives, Account Managers and service delivery and channel partners.
  • Ensure effective handover to Customer Success and Channel teams, documenting the proposed solution, technical dependencies, customer expectations and deployment considerations.
  • Bring customer feedback and integration requirements to Dropbox Product teams and leadership to inform product improvements and priorities.
  • Travel to customer sites, conferences and other relevant events as required.

Requirements

  • 6+ years of experience as a Sales Engineer, Solutions Consultant, Professional Services Solutions Consultant or in a comparable customer-facing technical role.
  • Demonstrable hands-on experience using REST APIs and at least one programming or scripting language to build, test and troubleshoot integrations. Ability to explain authentication, data flows, technical decisions and your personal contribution to delivered solutions.
  • Strong technical expertise in SaaS applications and integrations across cloud-hosted and on-premises environments, including collaboration or productivity technologies.
  • Experience implementing large-scale IT projects, SaaS solutions or enterprise deployments, translating customer requirements into workable technical solutions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience explaining technical concepts, business value and trade-offs to technical teams, executives and other key stakeholders.
  • Deep understanding of identity management and authentication, including experience integrating with technologies such as Okta, Azure AD, Active Directory and SAML 2.0.
  • Solid understanding of security and networking technologies, including CASBs, SIEMs and/or DLPs, and their implications for enterprise SaaS adoption and integrations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting API-led SaaS platforms, data platforms, cloud infrastructure or cloud storage solutions, including object storage such as Amazon S3.
  • Experience addressing customer use cases in media and entertainment, AI or security.
  • Understanding of workplace transformation trends and their implications for enterprise workflows, collaboration and technology adoption.

location: San Francisco, CA • New York, NY • United States
text:

Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

Figma employees are among the most AI-active in the industry, and our Internal AI team, part of FTS (our Business Technology org), helps turn that energy into meaningful impact by making it easier for every Figmate, from Sales and Support to Finance, People, and Legal, to safely adopt AI and use it to improve how they work. 

We’re a small, high-leverage team organized around three pillars: Platform & Tooling, Infrastructure & Hosting, and Applied AI Builds, and this role is a key member of the Applied AI Builds pillar.

As an AI Engineer, Internal Tools, you’ll work directly with teams across Figma to identify high-value AI opportunities and take them to production, moving from understanding a business workflow, to rapidly prototyping an approach, to evaluating it and integrating it with the systems and data needed to make it useful in the real world. 

This isn’t a role focused only on building AI demos: you’ll own solutions through production, help determine where AI adds value and where traditional rules-based software is the right choice, and shape how agents can safely take actions across enterprise systems.   • Experience taking an AI application or workflow beyond a prototype and operating it in a production environment
  • Strong API, integration, and system design fundamentals, with experience connecting applications across multiple systems and data sources and strong engineering judgment about when to apply AI and when a rules-based approach is the right choice, and experience designing reliable production systems with appropriate observability, failure handling, authentication, authorization, and security controls

As a Compliance Engineer at Figma, you will play a critical role in designing, implementing, and testing security controls across multiple compliance frameworks, including FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and NIST. You will collaborate closely with security, infrastructure, and product engineering teams to translate regulatory requirements into effective technical controls, evaluate control effectiveness, and identify opportunities to improve security and compliance processes. You will also help advance Figma’s compliance engineering capabilities by leveraging automation, machine-readable control definitions (JSON), APIs, and AI-assisted development tools to streamline control testing, evidence collection, and continuous monitoring. This role combines deep security compliance expertise with technical problem-solving to build scalable, repeatable, and effective compliance practices.

This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

  • Design and execute control testing procedures to assess control performance, surface gaps, and verify that remediation is complete
  • Establish repeatable control assessments and continuous monitoring processes to evaluate compliance effectiveness
  • Translate security requirements into structured, machine-readable JSON definitions to support control management, testing, and automation
  • Build and maintain API integrations and automated workflows to streamline evidence collection, control validation, and compliance processes
  • Identify opportunities to improve control effectiveness, reduce manual effort, and scale compliance operations across multiple frameworks

  • Experience testing security controls for design and operating performance, including surfacing gaps and confirming fixes

Figma is building its founding Forward Deployed Engineering team to solve the complex, real-world challenges that emerge when bringing Figma’s products into large-scale enterprise environments and looking for founding Forward Deployed Engineers. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll embed directly with strategic customers, working across their codebases, design systems, developer environments, and workflows to make Figma’s products successful within their unique technical constraints. You’ll tackle the hardest adoption challenges hands-on, from complex frontend stacks and legacy systems to security and access requirements, while building trusted partnerships with customers’ senior engineering teams.

This is a senior/staff-level engineering role within Product and Engineering, not a sales or services function. You’ll work directly in customer environments when needed, using the minimum access required. Your goal is smooth adoption by the customer’s product and engineering teams, which means making complex workflows work simply in their environment and solving the underlying problems You’ll do that hands-on, often by writing Figma product code, then turn what you learn into a reusable path for future customers instead of taking permanent ownership of the customer’s codebase. Working closely with Figma’s Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Experience teams, you’ll help shape both the product and how this brand-new function works and scales. The role is highly collaborative, deeply customer-facing, and built for engineers who thrive in ambiguity, take end-to-end ownership, and want to solve the highest-impact problems at the intersection of product, engineering, and customer needs. This role includes periodic travel to work alongside strategic customers in person.

This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

What you'll do at Figma:

  • Make an enterprise design system agent-ready so AI tools generate faithful, on-system code: fix tokens, naming, and guidelines, wire up Code Connect, and run evals
  • Get Make Local, Code Layers, and our newest products working in a customer’s real environment, writing code, config, agent skills, and guideline files against their systems and ours
  • Run technical discovery: understand a customer's dev environment, toolchain, and constraints, then scope the fastest credible path to value, in addition to setting the customer up for long term success
  • Debug hard, unfamiliar integration problems (git workflows, CI, dev-environment setup, non-standard stacks)
  • Build LLM-powered workflows: MCP setup, agent skills, and prompt engineering tuned to each customer’s context
  • Turn one-off solutions into reusable playbooks and product feedback, so patterns you solve once become self-serve or shipped product
  • Bring  learnings on friction back to Figma's Product and Engineering teams, influence what gets built next, and often build it
