title: Support Engineering Manager - NAMER
text:
HELLO!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring our first Support Engineering Manager in AMER.

Support Engineering is the technical bridge between frontline Support, Product, and Engineering. The team investigates complex product and customer issues, helps confirm which problems truly require code changes, and enables the broader Support organization to resolve more issues independently. We’re looking for a hands-on leader to make that bridge stronger as the function grows—aligning technical rigor with Ashby’s broader standards for customer success.

This is not a traditional Support Manager role. You’ll manage and mentor Support Engineers, stay close to complex investigations, and work with Engineering and Product to improve how technical issues are diagnosed, escalated, and resolved. You’ll help define the standards and systems that let a small, highly technical team move quickly without sacrificing judgment or quality.




ABOUT THE ROLE

When a complex issue moves beyond frontline Support, Support Engineering investigates the problem using customer context, application behavior, logs, databases, integrations, APIs, and code-level context. The team determines whether the issue can be resolved through configuration, data correction, documentation, enablement, or an in-app change—or whether it is a product defect that Engineering needs to fix. Your role is to make that path clearer and more effective: develop a deep understanding of how each partner team works, coach the investigation, and ensure escalations meet a shared standard for evidence, ownership, and customer impact.

You’ll lead the team’s day-to-day technical development while building the connective tissue around it. That includes reviewing investigations and escalations, mentoring Support Engineers through ambiguous problems, clarifying triage and handoff practices, identifying recurring patterns, and partnering with frontline Support, Product, and Engineering on durable improvements. You’ll help ensure Support Engineering scales in a way that reflects Ashby’s broader expectations for customer success—not simply by passing issues between teams, but by resolving more issues independently and making the right problems easier for Engineering to act on.

As the first Support Engineering Manager at Ashby, you’ll have meaningful influence over how the function grows. You’ll balance people leadership with hands-on technical judgment, make pragmatic decisions with incomplete information, and focus the team on the work that most improves customer outcomes, strengthens cross-functional trust, and protects Engineering time.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Lead, coach, and develop Support Engineers through regular feedback, technical mentorship, career development, and clear expectations for ownership and judgment.

 - Stay close to complex investigations by reviewing technical work, joining escalations when useful, and coaching the team on APIs, integrations, logs, databases, data issues, configuration, and product behavior.

 - Build shared operating standards across Support, Support Engineering, Product, and Engineering that help frontline Support resolve more issues independently, reduce customer effort, and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable escalations when code changes are needed.

 - Partner with Engineering and Product to synthesize recurring customer patterns, validate defects, improve supportability, and determine whether the right solution is a code change, documentation, tooling, enablement, or process improvement.

 - Identify the highest-leverage friction in the team’s workflows and ship practical improvements to tooling, diagnostics, routing, documentation, and operating processes.

 - Hire and onboard future Support Engineers, help define the team’s career path, and build a scalable model for technical growth as the function expands across regions.

 - Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, frontline self-sufficiency, customer effort, recurring issue reduction, and Engineering time spent on confirmed defects and roadmap work.


YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

 - You have direct people-management experience leading a technical support, developer support, production support, or support engineering team in a B2B SaaS or similarly complex software environment.

 - You are energized by hands-on people leadership: reviewing work, giving precise feedback, raising technical judgment, and helping strong engineers grow.

 - You have coached an Engineer through a specific technical or judgment gap and can point to what changed as a result.

 - You have enough technical depth to reason about APIs, integrations, logs, databases, application behavior, and code-level context—and to coach others through ambiguous investigations.

 - You know how to distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect, and can help a team make that decision with evidence.

 - You have improved an escalation, triage, or support-to-Engineering workflow and can explain what changed, why you changed it, and how you measured the result.

 - You build structure without over-engineering. You can make clear decisions with incomplete information, ship a useful first version, and iterate based on what you learn. You’ve stood up processes, workflows, or standards from scratch.

 - You communicate clearly and thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences, especially when explaining tradeoffs, uncertainty, customer impact, and recommended action.


YOU SHOULD NOT APPLY IF

 - You have not yet directly managed a team, and your leadership experience has primarily been through mentorship, project leadership, or team-lead responsibilities. This role requires direct people-management experience, including accountability for team development, feedback, and day-to-day management.

 - You’re looking primarily for a traditional queue-management or people-management role where you can stay removed from technical investigations and escalation quality.

 - Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, infrastructure, cloud operations, or systems administration without substantial experience debugging customer-impacting SaaS applications and integrations.

 - You prefer to optimize processes from a distance rather than work directly with engineers on the details of diagnosis, evidence, and technical judgment.

 - You see Support Engineering primarily as a pass-through queue to Engineering rather than an investigation and enablement layer that should resolve more issues independently.

 - You’re uncomfortable operating in a growing function where ownership boundaries, workflows, and success measures will continue to evolve.

 - You prefer prolonged analysis or perfect certainty over making a well-reasoned decision, learning quickly, and improving the system in motion.




ABOUT ASHBY

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at  https://www.ashbyhq.com/ashbyhq.com http://ashbyhq.com.




ABOUT GO TO MARKET

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

 - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

 - We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

 - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-leadership-principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical leadership, people management, communication, judgment, and cross-functional collaboration.

 - Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min

 - Hiring Manager interview — 45 min

 - Take-home assessment - 5 days to complete

 - Support Leadership — 30 min

 - Founder interview — 30 min

 - Virtual Onsite — 75 min
   
   - Engineering Partnership — 30 min
   
   - Support Manager Partnership — 30 min
   
   - Closing Questions — 15 min




BENEFITS

Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby—do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - A $1,200 annual learning and professional-development budget.

 - A one-time $2,000 home-office setup budget for furniture, monitors, peripherals, and ergonomic equipment, plus a company-provided laptop.

 - Extended health benefits for you and your dependents (subject to availability with our Employer of Record)

 - Opportunities to spend time with teammates through an annual company offsite, team offsites, local meetups, and virtual events.

The People Operations Team provides support to Ashby employees through the development and implementation of programs, policies, and services that contribute to a productive and inclusive working environment. We ensure that the work we do aligns with our Operating Principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles#operating-principles and strengthens the environment we're building at Ashby. Our approach is to do things differently – we prioritize what truly fits our team and enhances how we work together. By embracing creativity and customization, we aim to create a people-first culture that drives both individual and organizational success.

We review all applications, and there isn’t a benefit to applying quickly. Take your time, look at the application questions and please submit before the application deadline! We aren’t able to take calls outside of the interview process, so reaching out to the team won’t push your application forward.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced Total Rewards leader to build and own Ashby’s total rewards function through our next phase of growth.

This is a builder’s role. Some of the foundation is in place; a lot of it isn’t. You’ll set the philosophy, design the frameworks, build the infrastructure, and run the work day to day. It’s a chance to shape how a company rewards its people rather than administer decisions someone else made.

It’s also unusually analytical, and unusually creative. Ashby’s Total Rewards philosophy is principled and intentionally not one-size-fits-all: approaches vary by function, because different parts of the business compete in different talent markets. Total Rewards partners closely with leadership to provide the structure, documentation, guidance, and governance that keep those approaches equitable, competitive, and scalable. The upshot is that the most interesting problems here don’t have off-the-shelf answers. How do you price a role that survey data doesn’t cover? How do you keep a flexible system fair and explainable? How do you tell, early, that one talent market has moved while the others haven’t? You’ll need real fluency with data, the discipline to structure a problem before you solve it, and the confidence to invent the model when no model exists.

A lot of this work looks less like administering a program and more like a well-run strategy engagement: frame the question, get the data, build the model, pressure-test the answer, and bring leaders a recommendation with the tradeoffs made explicit. The difference is that here you also go implement it.

You’ll partner closely with People Ops, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Legal, and functional leaders to design programs that support how Ashby attracts, retains, and rewards exceptional people — building a more scalable approach while preserving the flexibility each part of the business needs.

We’re looking for someone who has built and scaled Total Rewards in high-growth, VC-backed SaaS companies and is energized by all three of philosophy, systems, and execution — someone who would rather go build the analysis than wait for it.

This role starts as an individual contributor and is expected to grow into people management as the function scales.




YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

Building Ashby’s compensation infrastructure

Bands, leveling alignment, market positioning, review cadences, benchmarking methodology, and clear guidance for offers, promotions, refreshers, and market adjustments — globally, and in partnership with founders, executives, and functional leaders. Some areas are mature; others are still forming. You’ll bring structure to the ambiguity with frameworks that are principled, practical, and hold up under scrutiny. You will be responsible for helping leaders reason through tradeoffs, bringing them a clear recommendation and the logic behind it, and documenting the non-standard rather than handing anyone a rule book.

Reading the market and helping Ashby adapt quickly

Combine market data, internal data, and outside signals to allow us to respond quickly and at scale when conditions change. Build the mechanisms that catch market movement across the whole company, not just the functions with the loudest signals: find the gaps in survey coverage, spot which teams are repricing faster than others, form a view on why, and turn what you see into a recommendation.

Owning Total Rewards strategy end-to-end

Compensation, equity, benefits, and perks. With founders and company leaders, define the philosophy, principles, and long-term direction for how we reward people globally. Evaluate our programs continuously and make recommendations that balance market competitiveness, internal equity, business needs, and long-term sustainability — framed the way a good strategy memo is framed: the options, the tradeoffs, and where you land.

Leading benefits strategy and administration

Own global benefits end to end: strategy, selection, renewals, plan design, competitiveness assessment, broker and vendor management, and the systems and processes behind a strong employee experience.

Leading equity program infrastructure

Partner with Finance and company leadership to bring structure, consistency, and scalability to equity practices, support program administration, and help employees understand how equity fits within the broader Total Rewards picture.

Building scalable systems and operations

Improve the systems, workflows, documentation, and operational processes behind Total Rewards. You will work in tools like CandorIQ, Pave, and OpenComp. You will use automation, AI, and good operational design to get roles to market quickly, support pay decisions efficiently, and keep the underlying data trustworthy.

Acting as a trusted cross-functional partner

You’re the subject matter expert for Total Rewards at Ashby. You’ll help leaders navigate rewards decisions with sound judgment, fairness, and clarity — and make complicated questions land simply in front of founders and executives.

Preparing the function to scale

You begin as a hands-on functional owner, but you’ll build with future scale in mind by establishing the documentation, operating rhythms, standards, and decision-making frameworks the function will need as it grows, and flagging the organizational needs ahead.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You bring several years of progressive Total Rewards experience, including meaningful ownership of compensation, benefits, and equity programs in high-growth organizations and you’ve built compensation infrastructure from the ground up.

 - You bring an analytical first mindset. You build the model, pressure-test your own numbers, and would rather run the analysis yourself than wait for someone else to.

 - You’re a structured thinker. You take a messy question, break it into the parts that matter, form a hypothesis, and test it — and you can walk someone through your reasoning without losing them.

 - You’re a creative problem solver in the comp space. When benchmarks are thin or the role is new, you reason from first principles and design the approach that fits the problem and not the one you used last time.

 - You’re comfortable where some principles are centralized and other elements are tailored by function, and you can keep that flexibility equitable and explainable.

 - You’ve built and scaled compensation frameworks and benefits programs for globally distributed organizations, ideally through periods of significant growth.

 - You can support leaders with different needs and viewpoints while holding the line on trust, consistency, and decision quality.

 - You’re highly effective at both strategy and execution, and comfortable being the primary owner of the work day to day.

 - You’re an exceptional communicator who can make complex Total Rewards topics land with any audience and can show the reasoning behind a number, not just the number. You’re comfortable putting a recommendation in front of founders and defending it.

 - You’re detail-oriented and operationally strong, always looking for ways to improve systems, processes, and program quality.

 - You’ve led or managed others, or you’re excited to build and eventually scale a Total Rewards team.


BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience building and scaling global compensation and benefits programs across multiple regions and employment models.

 - Experience using automation, AI, and technology to make Total Rewards operations faster, more accurate, and more scalable.

 - Strong modeling and data skills beyond the standard toolkit including advanced spreadsheet work, SQL, Python, or BI tools.

 - A background that blends Total Rewards with strategy consulting, corporate finance or FP&A, or people analytics. We value people who have been trained to structure and solve ambiguous problems, wherever they learned to do it.

 - Experience with tools such as CandorIQ, Pave, and OpenComp.


THIS ROLE MAY NOT BE A FIT IF

 - You want to bring your own Total Rewards playbook and install it at Ashby, rather than reimagine and evolve what’s already been started.

 - You prefer operating inside highly standardized programs to building and adapting them in a more flexible environment.

 - You’re less interested in the hands-on work of running the function — including doing the analysis yourself.

 - You reach for the benchmark before the reasoning, or you need rigid rules to make a call.

 - You’d rather present the data than the recommendation.

 - You’re uncomfortable making decisions in ambiguity or helping leaders through nuanced compensation questions.

 - Your experience is concentrated in one area of Total Rewards, with limited exposure across compensation, equity, and benefits.

 - You’re not energized by partnering across functions, balancing competing perspectives, and shaping practical solutions.

 - Most of your experience is in mature organizations with established programs, processes, and teams, without having had to build infrastructure through growth and change.


INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is thorough — we aim to ensure each person joining the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows:

 - Recruiter Screen with Talent Acquisition Team - 30 minutes

 - Hiring Manager Interview - 45 minutes

 - Take Home Assignment
   
   - Followed by 1 hour live session to discuss

 - Virtual Onsite - 2.5-3 hours

 - Final Round with CEO - 30 minutes


ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of recruiting software and we’re starting with a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run an efficient and data-driven hiring process. We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom.  We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅.

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

title: Manager of Strategic Customer Success
text:
Hi, I’m Loren https://www.linkedin.com/in/lfoseid/, the Head of Strategic Customer Success here at Ashby. My team is dedicated to building deep, consultative partnerships within the Enterprise space. One of our operating principles is “Aim High” and I'm excited to find a Manager of Strategic Customer Success who can identify gaps, drive meaningful change, and bring a creative vision to this segment as we scale.

In this role, you'll lead a team of CSMs who serve Ashby's largest and most complex customers. A key part of this role is helping your team navigate the nuances of enterprise partnerships — building the depth of engagement these customers expect while identifying what's working and translating it into repeatable approaches that scale across a sophisticated book of business. You'll partner closely with other leaders across Product, Implementation, Support, and Contract Management.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Manager of Strategic Customer Success, you'll lead a tenured team of skilled CSMs while helping shape how Ashby delivers value as we scale upmarket. You'll be the team's coach, sounding board, and champion — helping CSMs grow, building systems that scale, and advocating cross-functionally — all in service of helping customers drive exceptional outcomes with a rapidly evolving product.

As our Manager of Strategic Customer Success, you’ll:

 - Lead and coach a team of CSMs who serve as the primary point of contact for customers post-onboarding and throughout the partnership

 - Uplevel team performance through 1:1 coaching, skill development, and operational rigor

 - Drive process optimization across the customer journey — with a particular focus on adoption and optimization

 - Advocate for the CSM team cross-functionally across Product, Support, Sales, RevOps, and Contract Management

 - Balance building scalable process with delivering the bespoke experiences our most complex customers expect

 - Be a key voice in evolving how we deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes for our Enterprise customers


ROLE REQUIREMENTS:

 - Team Leadership & Coaching: You have experience leading and developing Customer Success Managers in a SaaS environment. You know how to foster a culture of empathy, accountability, and continuous growth.

 - Technical Acumen: You're able to get into the technical details of the product alongside your direct reports to help drive customer solutions, and you have experience coaching teams that support a technically complex product.

 - Customer Journey Expertise: You understand the enterprise customer lifecycle and have helped improve onboarding, adoption, and retention through thoughtful, repeatable approaches.

 - Up Market Motion: You have worked with enterprise customers and scaled their use case as they grow in complexity.

 - Operational Mindset: You’ve helped implement and improve team processes, and you bring a structured lens to scaling what works while staying adaptable.

 - Cross-functional Collaboration: You’re comfortable partnering with teams like Sales, Product, and Support to align around customer needs and elevate the experience.

 - Problem-Solving Orientation: You don’t rely on “what worked before” — you’re thoughtful, pragmatic, and eager to find solutions that fit the unique needs of your team and customers.

 - Data-Driven: You are comfortable using data and metrics to drive decision-making, continually improving both the team and customer experience.

 - Customer-First Thinking: You have a deep understanding of B2B customer needs and have a history of ensuring outstanding support experiences.

 - Lifecycle Awareness: You understand the full customer lifecycle, and know how to effectively partner with cross-functional teams to ensure strong handoffs and sustained success.


YOU’LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU:

 - You demonstrate clear communication. You ask clarifying questions with precision and can distill complex concepts into simple, actionable themes.

 - You listen deeply. You see your role as both an advocate for the Customer Success team and a voice of the customer to internal stakeholders — ensuring our product roadmap continues to evolve in the right direction.

 - You advocate for your team. You engage actively in resourcing and headcount planning conversations and bring a clear point of view.

 - You love to coach. You see every teaching moment as an opportunity and are excited to help your team grow and develop.

 - You are a structured problem solver. You thrive at solving complex challenges with innovative, scalable solutions.

 - You know process matters. You are eager to improve processes and workflows to enhance efficiency and efficacy.

 - Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You take pride in strong internal operations.


YOU MIGHT NOT BE A FIT IF:

 - Getting into the details isn't your thing. Call shadowing, hands-on troubleshooting, and doing the work alongside your direct reports isn't appealing.

 - Getting deep in the product and being a technical resource for your direct reports is not interesting to you.

 - You're more comfortable generating broad ideas than owning their execution.

 - You prefer established, stable processes and find frequent change frustrating.

 - You want to build something once and move on, rather than continuously iterate and improve on it.

 - You primarily work with simple products, not highly configurable complex products

 - You have not spent the last few years leading an upmarket Customer Success team in a growing B2B SaaS business


ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. Learn more on our website:  https://www.ashbyhq.com/%EF%BF%BC%EF%BF%BCWehttps://www.ashbyhq.com/

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀




OUR PHILOSOPHY

Here are a few key points (relevant to the go-to-market side) that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

 - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is a lot easier to sell.

 - We want to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers which requires a deep understanding of the Ashby product, even leadership roles.

 - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people (and the right work environment) deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We hire and compensate accordingly.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process.


THE INTERVIEW

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety:

30 min - Recruiter Screen

45 min - Hiring Manager Interview with Head of Strategic Customer Success

Presentation Round

Final Round

 - You get to work with a product that our prospects & customers are truly excited about.

 - Competitive compensation is offered.

title: Data Analytics Manager
text:
ABOUT THIS ROLE

👋 Hi, I’m Kevin https://www.linkedin.com/in/adamantine/. I manage the Data team and our analytics products at Ashby. I’m hiring our first Data Analytics Manager at an important point in Ashby’s growth, and I hope you have the patience to read a job posting that may be a little unconventional.

You will manage Ashby’s three Data Analysts: two core analysts and one analyst focused on Revenue Operations. Our Data Engineer will initially continue to report directly to me, so this role is deliberately more focused on the analytical side of the team while remaining a close partner in the broader data ecosystem.

The primary result of your successful management will be a team of analysts with excellent judgment, strong technical methods, clear communication, and a deep sense of ownership. I am looking for someone who can help that team do better work, choose better work, and grow into the next stage of Ashby alongside the company.

Rather than begin with a long list of tools or years of experience, I want to share four questions that sit at the center of this role. If you apply, your answer should be “yes” to each. Should we get a chance to talk, what I will really want to understand is the nuance: your unique how, why, and what behind your answers.

 1. Can you identify and hire talented people?
    
    We will continue to grow the analyst team, and you will play a meaningful role in finding and assessing future teammates. Great analysts combine technical judgment, curiosity, communication, business context, and a willingness to own work end to end. Can you recognize that combination in others?

 2. Can you develop and amplify the data practices that let a small team do excellent work?
    
    Ashby’s Data team is lean, and our practices will need to evolve as the company becomes more complex. I see this role as an opportunity to improve the ways we prioritize work, review it, share knowledge, maintain quality, and collaborate.

 3. Can you lead the team through the transition from broad shared context to meaningful specialization?
    
    Today, each analyst can know a great deal about the company and data stack. That will become more challenging as Ashby grows across products, regions, systems, and business functions. We will need to develop stronger domain context and clearer ways of working without turning the team into a set of narrow, disconnected specialists.

 4. Can you help the Data team navigate the rapidly evolving implications of AI?
    
    AI will affect how our analysts work, how the company self-serves analytical questions, and how other teams use internal business data. Much of that work depends on trusted, well-modeled, appropriately accessible warehouse-derived data. You will help the Data team explore and evaluate the relevant tools, workflows, and partnerships—bringing ambition, practicality, and a high bar for accuracy.

These questions add up to a simple reality: Ashby is growing quickly, and the surrounding data needs are becoming more complex. We are becoming a multi-product, global company with more business systems and larger team dynamics. This is a great opportunity at a great company, but it will be hard and consequential work. I am looking for a manager who is excited to help shape the Data function and build an excellent team for its current and future members.



YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES AS A DATA ANALYTICS MANAGER

To understand the role, it helps to understand how our team works today.

Data Analysts at Ashby are full-stack members of the Data team. We do not have a traditional split where Analytics Engineers build models and Data Analysts perform analysis only on prepared datasets. Our analysts work across raw and modeled data, contribute to dbt models and metric definitions, conduct deep analysis, build dashboards and other internal data products, and collaborate directly with partners throughout the company.

As a rough sketch, the team receives work through a standardized request process. Anyone can make a request; we triage it, assess the actual need, and decide whether it can be addressed quickly or should become a more deliberate project with a kickoff and plan. We do not currently organize ourselves around universal SLAs, sprints, or points. Instead, we aim to be good partners: communicate clearly, assess capacity honestly, prioritize thoughtfully, and make deliberate choices about what not to do. You will have a lot of leverage in aiding this process well.

Ashby’s Operating Principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles place principled thinking ahead of reflexively leaning on prior experience or convention. In practice, that means work at Ashby does not always start with “let’s get all the data and metrics.” Data is one useful tool for resolving uncertainty; it is not automatically the first or only tool. That said, as the company matures and more teams optimize their work, demand for data will likely continue to grow. You will help us meet that demand with good judgment.



WHY YOU SHOULD OR SHOULDN’T APPLY

At Ashby’s current size, this is a player-coach role. You should expect to get hands-on with analytical work as you learn the business and the team, and to remain close enough to the work to guide its quality well.

You could be a strong fit if you:

 - Have exceptional analytical judgment. You can calibrate the depth and rigor of an analysis to the decision at hand: knowing when precision matters, when uncertainty is material, and when additional work would not change the outcome.

 - Can produce and evaluate transparent, rigorous analysis. You bring readers along through the problem context, data considered, assumptions, meaningful cleaning or reduction steps, caveats, statistical pitfalls, and practical conclusion.

 - Are a strong visual and written communicator. You care about clear tables and charts, meaningful labels and definitions, coherent narratives, and making complex work understandable without overstating certainty.

 - Have deep hands-on SQL experience, plus working fluency with dbt-style data modeling, cloud data warehouses, and BI tools. You do not need to have owned a warehouse as a Data Engineer, but you should be comfortable working across the analytical data stack.

 - Have led, managed, or functionally acted as a manager for data practitioners in a high-growth company. Formal people-management experience is valuable, but not required if you have demonstrated equivalent judgment, coaching, hiring, and team-leadership abilities.

 - Bring a product-manager-like instinct for finding the core need behind a request, understanding users and business context, and turning ambiguous questions into useful work.

 - Are pragmatic and intellectually flexible. You see data as one important input to good judgment alongside qualitative research, collaboration, user understanding, and clear thinking.

 - Are intimately familiar with the B2B SaaS industry, workflows and organizational structures.

 - Have an eye and instinct for simplicity over complexity in all matters.

 - Have experience in a growth-stage, product-oriented technology company and are energized by helping a lean team scale.

 - You can appreciate the whole distribution as much as a point estimator.


PUT ANOTHER WAY, YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY IF:

 - You are looking for a pure-management role removed from the details of analytical work. You will need to be comfortable getting hands-on as you learn the team and helping analysts work through difficult problems.

 - You have only worked in an environment where analysis begins after another team has fully prepared the data. Ashby analysts are expected to work across the stack, from modeling through final analysis and dashboards.

 - Spreadsheet-only analytical work is your preferred mode. Fluency with SQL in a modern data warehouse is essential.

 - You would rather use a metric, dashboard, experiment, or process by default than first ask what degree of evidence is actually needed to make a good decision.

 - You are looking for consumer-scale data infrastructure projects. We have a large and interesting dataset (see our Talent Trends https://www.ashbyhq.com/talent-trends-report reports!), but we are a B2B SaaS company. Relative to many B2C services, we are small but mighty.

 - You are seeking an in-person work experience. Ashby is remote, although there are employee hotspots around the world and we meet in person at various events throughout the year.

 - You have never formally managed a data team.

Naturally, this role is important and represents a combination of different skills. You may not meet every dimension perfectly, and that’s OK. If the dot product of your skill vector with this requirements vector is close to 1, please consider applying, but please note it does not have to be 1.0.



DATA CULTURE AT ASHBY

At Ashby, we draw a clear distinction between when to look to data for "the answer" and when to use data to aid principled thinking for decision making. In general, a primary consideration is whether or not data is needed to help clarify points of uncertainty. When data is considered necessary, a secondary consideration is to what depth data will be required. Data questions lend themselves to ongoing "what about..." or "what if..." explorations, which can be important in some situations but are not always necessary.

With these dynamics in mind, we do not foster an environment where every decision we make should be backed by data, but we do foster an environment where teammates ask whether or not data will fit the task at hand well. This, in turn, allows us to operate a lean team focused on projects where data provides true leverage to our overall business and product goals.

As a related but distinct point, Ashby’s data culture, as far as transparency and access goes, is very open. We share company-wide access to our financial standings, progress, goals, and generally make any data and reporting results broadly available. Outside of constraints related to whether a teammate has access to a particular tool, there are close to no constraints on access the state of the company as told by data or reporting. In general, we would like to continue and extend open access to data throughout the company (with your help!), but with consideration and not as a substitute for principled thinking :)




INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is thorough, but we aim to be respectful of the total candidate time invested. We aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to determine if Ashby is the right fit for you. The expected process for this role is as follows:

 - Hiring Manager Screen (30 mins)

 - Technical Screen (45 min)

 - Assessment: Mini Analysis and Write-up (45min)

 - Final Round - Virtual Onsite (~2.5, can be split into multiple days)
   
   - (45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Productivity
   
   - (45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Collaboration
   
   - (30 mins) Business Partnership
   
   - (30 mins) Chat with a Founder
   
   - (15 mins) Follow-Up Conversation + Debrief with the Hiring Manager

Note: please do not reach out to the broader Ashby team requesting more information or time to connect. We will diligently review all applications in detail after the public posting period is over.



BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby - do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

 - A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.


If you've made it this far and are excited about Ashby, please apply and follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/ashbyhq to stay up to date!

title: GTM Systems Analyst
text:
THE ROLE

Ashby's GTM engine runs on a set of interconnected systems. Keeping them accurate, efficient, and trusted is the foundation everything else is built on. As our GTM Systems Analyst, you'll own the daily maintenance and configuration of technical layer that powers our Go-to-Market organization: the CRM configurations, integration architecture, and data quality practices that let our Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams move fast with confidence.

This role sits within Revenue Operations, the horizontal function that makes the entire GTM system work. You'll be embedded in daily operations (triaging issues, implementing new tooling, and translating business requirements into scalable configurations) while also contributing to longer-term systems strategy as we move up-market and expand our product suite.




WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS NOW

We're in an active expansion phase: new products, new segments, new GTM motions. Our systems need to keep pace. The person in this role will shape how we build the technical foundation for the next chapter of Ashby's growth.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - System Administration: Own the day-to-day health of our core GTM platforms. You'll manage configuration, user permissions, custom objects, and workflow automation across our CRM stack — making sure the systems actually reflect how our teams work, not just how they were set up two years ago.

 - Integration Support: Maintain clean data flows across our GTM toolset ( including intent data, conversation intelligence, and sales engagement platforms). You'll be the person who knows how signals travel between systems and why, and who makes sure they're flowing reliably.

 - Data Governance: Enforce standards for data quality, deduplication, and field taxonomy. Revenue reporting and forecasting are only as good as the data underneath them, along with our GTM Engineers and our System Architect, you'll build the infrastructure of trust that makes those outputs credible.

 - Stakeholder Support: Be the go-to technical partner for frontline GTM teams. You'll triage issues, gather business requirements, and deliver solutions that scale. You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical partners and know when to say "that requires a bigger conversation" rather than patching around a root cause.

 - Tooling Evaluation: Help evaluate new GTM tech and AI tools as our needs evolve. You'll assess how new tools will integrate with our existing systems, support contract renewals, and support implementation of emerging solutions, with a practical bias toward what will actually get adopted and maintained.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Advanced proficiency in CRM administration: Salesforce Administrator or HubSpot Administrator certification strongly preferred

 - Experience connecting marketing automation, CRM, and revenue intelligence tools (e.g., 6sense, Gong, Outreach, Gainsight)

 - Ability to translate abstract business goals into documented, scalable technical configurations

title: Senior Paid Marketing Manager
text:
Hi 👋 I'm Harriet, and I lead Marketing at Ashby.

We've built a business with 5,500+ customers, a highly differentiated product, and a brand that people genuinely care about. We've invested in content, customer stories, community, and the foundations of a strong marketing program. Now, we have an opportunity to build a much bigger paid engine to support our next stage of growth.

We're looking for a Senior Paid Marketing Manager to build it.

You'll take ownership of our existing LinkedIn program and expand across Meta, Google Search, YouTube, and other channels. You'll have meaningful budget, strong creative and technical partners, and the autonomy to build a program that creates qualified pipeline and strengthens our brand.

This is a hands-on role. We want someone who knows their channels inside out, enjoys getting into the details, and can take a campaign from initial hypothesis through execution, analysis, and optimization. You'll have access to specialist support when it makes sense, but you'll be the person driving the work.

We also believe AI creates an opportunity for exceptional individual contributors to do work that previously required much larger teams. We're looking for someone who is already exploring that opportunity and wants to push it further.




WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE INTERESTING

You get to build with the resources most marketers wish they had.

Paid is relatively underdeveloped at Ashby compared with the scale of our business. You get to build something substantial without unwinding years of accumulated complexity or fighting for the resources to make it work. We have strong content, customer proof, product differentiation, and an established brand. You'll start with a monthly budget in the hundreds of thousands of dollars and the support of our design, web, and RevOps teams.


YOU CAN RETHINK HOW PAID MARKETING GETS DONE.

We want to enable exceptional individual contributors to accomplish more through AI, automation, and better workflows. You'll have the freedom to experiment with new tools, build systems that improve your output, and challenge established ways of working.


YOU'LL BUILD A PROGRAM THAT MAKES THE BRAND AND BUSINESS STRONGER.

We believe great paid marketing combines analytical rigor with creative judgment. You'll optimize for pipeline and efficiency while building campaigns that earn attention, communicate our differentiation, and give the right buyers a reason to care about Ashby. We don't want a lead-generation machine that makes our brand worse.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Build and scale our paid program. Own strategy and execution across LinkedIn, Meta, and Google Search, expanding into YouTube and other channels as opportunities emerge. Prioritize audiences, develop campaign hypotheses, manage budgets, and turn promising experiments into repeatable sources of qualified pipeline.

Drive creative strategy and experimentation. Develop campaign concepts, write ad copy, brief creative, and shape landing-page tests. Work closely with design, content, and product marketing to produce distinctive work. Build a disciplined testing cadence across audiences, creative, offers, and conversion paths, knowing when to scale, iterate, or stop.

Use AI to increase your impact. Build practical workflows using AI, agents, and automation to improve research, creative iteration, campaign operations, and analysis. We want someone who actively experiments with new approaches, evaluates their effectiveness, and turns what works into repeatable systems.

Own measurement and performance. Drive our approach to paid measurement in partnership with RevOps. Establish the signals and reporting needed to understand qualified reach, conversion, pipeline contribution, and efficiency. Develop better ways to assess incrementality, make informed decisions with imperfect attribution, and translate performance data into clear investment recommendations.

Connect campaigns to the buyer journey. Partner with sales, lifecycle, and ABM to understand what makes an opportunity valuable and how paid can influence the journey from first touch through pipeline. Adapt messaging and investment to our customer segments and markets.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON IN YOUR FIRST SIX MONTHS

 - Take ownership of LinkedIn, identifying opportunities to improve qualified reach, creative, and progression into pipeline.

 - Build and scale Meta, establishing a strong creative testing cadence and the landing pages and follow-up needed to make the channel work.

 - Expand Google Search and launch YouTube, evaluating additional channels where there's a compelling audience and learning opportunity.

 - Establish a stronger operating system for paid, including AI-enabled workflows, measurement, and a clear approach to allocating investment.

The goal isn't to scale every channel equally. It's to build a broad set of opportunities, learn quickly, and concentrate investment where the evidence is strongest.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We care more about what you've built and how you think than the number of years you've spent in marketing.

 - You're a domain expert in paid media. You have deep, hands-on expertise in LinkedIn, Meta, and Google Ads. You understand the platforms, know how to structure and optimize campaigns, and can explain how your decisions have influenced qualified pipeline. You've personally built and scaled programs in sales-led B2B SaaS.

 - You're a builder, not just a strategist. You're excited to get into the accounts, develop the creative, run experiments, investigate performance, and solve problems yourself. You know when external expertise can help, but you don't need an agency to do the core work.

 - You combine analytical rigor with creative taste. You understand performance metrics and experimentation, but you also know what makes advertising compelling. You can connect campaign decisions to buyer quality and pipeline without losing sight of the brand you're building.

 - You're already changing how you work with AI. You can demonstrate how you've used AI tools, agents, or automation to improve your output. You think critically about where automation helps, how to evaluate its results, and how to turn useful experiments into repeatable workflows.

 - You take ownership of measurement. You can work with CRM data, establish useful performance reporting, investigate attribution limitations, and drive better measurement approaches rather than waiting for someone else to provide the answers. You own budgeting and explain the case for reallocating investment.

 - You're a strong cross-functional partner. You work well with sales, design, content, product marketing, and RevOps. You seek out context, share what you learn, and care about the overall customer experience rather than optimizing your own channel in isolation.

Experience with YouTube, display, and programmatic is valuable, as is familiarity with HubSpot and measurement platforms like Dreamdata. You don't need to have mastered every channel, but you should have the expertise and judgment to expand beyond your core strengths.




THIS ISN'T THE RIGHT ROLE FOR YOU IF

 - You prefer managing agencies to building campaigns. You want to set the strategy and have other people execute it, rather than getting into the details yourself.

 - You measure success primarily through platform metrics. You're satisfied with lower CPCs or more leads without understanding whether you're reaching the right buyers or contributing to pipeline.

 - You treat brand and performance as separate disciplines. You optimize individual campaigns without considering how the work shapes a prospect's perception of Ashby or contributes to long-term demand.

 - You haven't meaningfully changed how you work with AI. You're interested in the topic but haven't experimented with workflows, tools, or automation that improve your output.

 - You rely on other people to supply the ideas. You need a content team to hand you finished assets, a creative team to develop every concept, or an agency to tell you what to test next.

 - You prefer a proven playbook to an open-ended problem. You'd rather repeat an established formula than question assumptions, explore new opportunities, and work out what makes sense for this business.

 - You optimize your channel at the expense of the bigger picture. You don't enjoy collaborating with other teams or taking responsibility for the experience beyond the ad click.

We want someone who takes real pride in their craft, is generous with their expertise, and is excited to build something that the whole team can be proud of.




THE TOOLS YOU'LL WORK WITH

Our core stack includes LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, HubSpot, and Dreamdata, alongside AI-assisted tools for research, creative development, analysis, and automation.

title: Director of Knowledge Management - NAMER
text:
HELLO!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. 👋 Knowledge is one of the most important levers we have for delivering a great customer experience. Our knowledge ecosystem shapes how customers learn Ashby, how our Specialists resolve tickets, and how many customers never need to file a ticket at all. We have a tenured, talented Knowledge Management team doing excellent work. What we’re missing is someone to unify its work into a single, strategic practice.

That’s why we’re hiring our first Director of Knowledge Management. You’ll lead a team of Knowledge Managers and expand the team into new areas, including Digital Support experience and content localization.

You’ll set the vision, standards, and operating model that connect our customer-facing Help Center, internal Knowledge Base, and the self-service and in-app experiences built on them, including our AI Assistant. You’ll coach and develop a team that is growing and taking on new kinds of work, and you’ll be the voice of Knowledge in conversations with Support, Customer Success, Product, Engineering, and beyond.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

Today, our Knowledge Managers divide their work between internal and external content. You’ll help the team decide where to focus next, in what order, and how its structure should evolve to deliver on those priorities.

Knowledge Management is its own function at Ashby, separate from the internal and external enablement teams. You’ll build strong partnerships with both, defining clear boundaries and handoffs so content is consistent, never duplicated, and never left without an owner.

Your team will also co-own the AI Assistant’s self-service experience with Product, helping customers find the right knowledge when and where they need it. You’ll stay close enough to the content to coach with specifics, while relying on your team for the day-to-day execution of knowledge governance.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN:

Set the Direction for Knowledge

 - Define the vision, roadmap, and success measures for Knowledge Management across internal and external content.

 - Identify the highest-impact opportunities to improve the knowledge ecosystem and sequence them against team capacity.

 - Build a clear model for content ownership, governance, and quality, streamlining how content is created, reviewed, and kept current as our product evolves.

 - Champion Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) practices and drive adoption across Support.

Lead and Develop the Team

 - Coach and develop Knowledge Managers through specific feedback on their work, clear career paths, and growth opportunities.

 - Evolve the team’s structure and divide work in the way that best serves customers and the business, with room to move beyond the current internal/external split.

 - Hire and onboard new team members next year, including Knowledge Managers, a Digital Support experience role, and a localization role.

Shape the AI Assistant’s Self-Service Experience

 - Co-own the AI Assistant’s self-service experience with Product, aligning on strategy, roadmap, and quality and partnering with Support, Support Operations, and Engineering on design and testing.

 - Help lead both declarative flows (structured, designed paths) and generative flows (AI-composed answers grounded in our content), and decide when each is the right tool.

 - Shape how content is structured, tagged, and governed so the Assistant surfaces accurate, current answers.

Build Our Localization Strategy

 - Build our localization strategy for Help Center content and drive the translation strategy for Customer Education, balancing quality, speed, and cost.

 - Define priorities for languages, content types, and tooling, and put processes in place to keep translated content in sync with the source.

Measure and Improve Results

 - Define and report on knowledge health, including content usage, search success, deflection, article quality, freshness, and the impact of knowledge on ticket volume and handle time. Treat deflection as a signal of customer success, not just cost reduction.

 - Measure how well the AI Assistant resolves customer questions, and use those conversations, ticket trends, customer feedback, and Specialist input to identify gaps and set content priorities.

Partner Across Ashby

 - Work closely with Customer Education and internal enablement in RevOps to align on ownership, standards, and a shared view of the customer and employee learning journey.

 - Partner with Product Marketing and Engineering so documentation keeps pace with releases and launches.




REQUIREMENTS

 - Multiple years of experience leading knowledge management or content programs, setting strategy and building processes that scale with the business, ideally in B2B SaaS Support or Customer Experience.

 - Experience managing a team of content or knowledge professionals, including coaching people at different levels of experience.

 - Ability to connect knowledge across internal and external audiences, aligning Support, Product, Marketing, Engineering, and enablement teams around clear ownership and shared standards.

 - Experience designing or operating self-service or AI-assisted support experiences, including both structured and generative flows, and a point of view on how knowledge quality shapes their performance.

 - Experience defining success measures for knowledge and using data to prioritize and make tradeoffs.

 - Comfort working in ambiguity as the function’s first dedicated leader, building on existing practices while setting a clear direction.

 - Strong writing and editing instincts. You’ll stay close enough to the work to set a high quality bar and give specific feedback.

 - Experience with KCS or comparable methodologies.




YOU SHOULD APPLY IF:

 - You’ve led a knowledge management, documentation, or content program and managed a team of knowledge or content professionals.

 - You’ve designed or operated self-service or AI-assisted support experiences, including structured and generative flows, and understand how knowledge quality affects their performance.

 - You’re a strong writer and editor who can give specific feedback on the work, coach people at different levels, and help them grow.

 - You see knowledge as a strategic lever for customer experience and can bring teams together around clear ownership, shared standards, and measurable results.

 - You’re excited to build on an experienced team, shape how the function operates, and expand into new areas like Digital Support experience and localization.

 


YOU SHOULD NOT APPLY IF:

 - Your background doesn’t include both managing a knowledge or content team and setting strategy for a knowledge, documentation, or content program.

 - You haven’t designed or operated self-service or AI-assisted support experiences.

 - You want a purely strategic role that keeps you removed from the content and the detailed feedback your team needs.

 - You need a fully built, fully staffed function or an established playbook to step into. We have a strong foundation, but several roles are still to be hired and the operating model is still taking shape.

 - You want sole ownership of AI product decisions or prefer to work only within a team you manage. This role depends on shared decisions with Product and strong partnerships across Ashby.

 


ABOUT ASHBY

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com http://ashbyhq.com.

title: Demo Engineer
text:
ABOUT THIS ROLE

As Ashby’s first Demo Engineer, you’ll own the systems that make our demo environments reliable, current, and tailored — the infrastructure the entire go-to-market team leans on to show Ashby at its best. Today, AEs and SEs maintain and configure their own demo accounts by hand. That doesn’t scale: reps lose selling time, demos drift out of date, and every new product release widens the gap between what Ashby can do and what we can actually show live. Your job is to close that gap.

This is a net-new role. Right now, the work is split between ad hoc effort and a new set of disposable demo templates the Internal Platform team is building. You’ll own the layer on top of that foundation — customizing and extending those templates, generating realistic demo data, tailoring environments for specific verticals and new markets, and making sure every feature is demoable before it ships. You’ll sit within Solutions Engineering, reporting to the Global Head of Solutions Engineering, and partner closely with Internal Platform and Product teams.

Your work will be split roughly 70/30: about 70% owning, customizing, and extending the demo template system and the data and content inside it, and about 30% running demo readiness as a program — release readiness, documentation, and enablement so the GTM team always has current, credible demos to work with.

The best person for this job is genuinely hands-on technical — working with internal tools and configuration files, using APIs, and general data preparation — who gets energy from building leverage for a whole team rather than fixing one demo at a time.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF:

 - 🛠 You’re comfortable working in JSON, calling REST / developer APIs, using AI tools, and scripting to configure and customize environments.

 - 🏗 You’re a builder, not just an operator. You get energy from creating systems and tooling that make a whole team more effective over time.

 - 🎥 You care deeply about demo quality. You understand what makes a product demo land, and you’re thoughtful about data realism and the narrative a demo needs to support.

 - 🧠 You have strong product intuition and can learn a deeply configurable product quickly, understanding how the different pieces connect.

 - 🔁 You have an iterative mindset. You like testing what works, refining over time, and improving based on what you learn from the field.

 - 🧩 You’re a systems thinker who would rather standardize and automate than manually repeat the same setup.

 - ⚡ You’re comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy a 0→1 role where the infrastructure is still being built around you.

 - 🤝 You partner well cross-functionally — with Engineering and with GTM — and can translate their needs into reliable systems.

 - 💙 You have empathy for the go-to-market teams you support and the Talent Acquisition space they sell into.




BONUS POINTS FOR:

 - 📊 You’ve built demo environments, demo data, or sandbox/trial environments at a SaaS company before.

 - 🧰 You’ve written automation scripts or tooling to generate data or configure environments at scale.

 - 🎬 You’ve built and maintained a library of reusable, templated environments or assets that others relied on.

 - 🤝 You have experience with HR tech, ATS workflows, or recruiting operations.




EXAMPLES OF THINGS YOU’LL WORK ON:

 - 🧱 Own the scaled demo system — customize and extend the demo environment infrastructure to support the GTM team.

 - 🗂 Generate realistic demo data — standardize and automate how demo environments are populated to eliminate manual setup.

 - 🎯 Build vertical- and market-specific demos — create tailored content for target verticals and additional languages as we move upmarket and expand internationally.

 - 🚦 Own demo readiness for new releases — make sure every feature is correctly configured and demoable in demo environments before it ships to GA.

 - 🧪 Stand up trial and sandbox environments — create templated environments prospects can use to test Ashby during the sales cycle.

 - 📚 Document how it all works — maintain clear documentation so the GTM team knows when and how to use each demo environment.




WHY BECOME A DEMO ENGINEER AT ASHBY?

You’ll define a role that doesn’t exist yet. This is a net-new role designed around a real business need. You won’t inherit a mature playbook — you’ll build the infrastructure that lets the whole GTM team demo at a higher level.

Your work will compound. A great live demo helps one deal. A reliable, current, well-documented demo system improves every demo the entire go-to-market team runs. If you like creating leverage, this role has a lot of it.

The product gives you something real to work with. Ashby has strong product-market fit, and that matters here. You’re not manufacturing excitement around a weak product — you’re making it effortless to show something that already resonates when it’s shown well.

You’ll sit at the intersection of Engineering and GTM. This is a rare blend of technical building and understanding what the field actually needs. You’ll help translate our product releases into live deals — and connect the two.

The surface area keeps growing. As we ship new features and expand into new product areas, new verticals, and new geographies, demo needs compound with each release. There is a lot to build, and it only gets more interesting.




REASONS YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY:

 - If you want to be customer-facing or closing deals, this isn’t the right role — the impact here happens behind the scenes.

 - If you’re not genuinely hands-on technical — comfortable in JSON, APIs, and data — the core of this job will be frustrating.

 - If you need a fully built environment and a finished playbook, the ambiguity of a 0→1 role with infrastructure still being built will feel uncomfortable.

 - If continuously maintaining and updating environments as the product changes sounds tedious rather than satisfying, this won’t be a fit.

 - If you’d rather build production product features than internal tooling and demo systems, you’ll likely want a different engineering role.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is thorough — we want to make sure this role is the right fit for you and that you’re the right fit for Ashby. Details on the process for this role will be shared by your recruiter.




BENEFITS

 - You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

 - Sell a product that our customers are truly excited about.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby — do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.




ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of recruiting software and we’re starting with a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run an efficient and data-driven hiring process.

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!).

We're in the talent acquisition software business. We run the end-to-end hiring process through our own platform, and ensure a level playing field for all candidates. We staff across regions rather than relying on on-call rotations; we’ll discuss the specific schedule for this opening during the process.




NOT SURE WHICH SUPPORT ROLE IS RIGHT FOR YOU?

We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles. 

 - Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes.

 - Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes.

Please choose the role that best reflects your experience and interests rather than applying to both. If another Support role seems like a closer match, we’ll consider that in our review.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect.

You’ll investigate issues end to end using tools such as Plain, GitHub, Datadog, databases, and the codebase. You won’t write the fix; you’ll give Engineering a well-validated escalation with reproduction steps, relevant evidence, customer impact, and a root-cause hypothesis when possible. You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements. As an early Support Engineer in EMEA, you’ll establish regional operating practices and handoff norms across European time zones while bringing EMEA customer patterns to a global team.

 - Build trusted working relationships with frontline Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers.

 - Establish EMEA coverage, handoff, and operating practices across European time zones while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team.

title: Manager, Technical Services
text:
MANAGER OF TECHNICAL SERVICES

Hi, I’m John and I’m the Head of Professional Services at Ashby. One of my favorite aspects of Ashby is our operating principle of Continuous Improvement https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles#8---implement-continuous-improvement. Coupled with our principle of caring deeply about our customers, we often find ourselves wondering ‘what is a better way to accomplish this’. That’s why I am thrilled to be hiring our first Technical Services Manager! As a leader on our growing Professional Services team (within Ashby’s Customer Success organization), you’ll have the opportunity to play a key role early in our customers’ journey, ultimately up-leveling the overall customer experience.

The Ashby team has grown rapidly over the last few years, and we're not slowing down: we now support thousands of customers, with ARR growing much faster than 100% year over year. As we scale upmarket, we are increasingly partnering with larger, highly complex organizations that bring sophisticated HR tech stacks requiring more customized integrations. To meet this demand, our technical services function is expanding quickly, and we are looking for our first dedicated leader to guide this talented group of individual contributors through our next phase of scale. We'll share more details once we meet, but you probably have a good idea as to why we're hiring for this role.




THE ROLE:

We’re looking for our first Manager of Technical Services to be the strategic anchor for Ashby’s expanding technical integration services. This role bridges two distinct technical engines: you will oversee specialized integration consultants dedicated to deep Workday integrations, as well as a team of technical solution consultants who build bespoke API solutions, craft custom recommendations, and deliver hands-on technical builds for our customers.

Six months in, success looks like having a highly efficient, scaled team that seamlessly handles multiple concurrent complex integrations, successfully troubleshoots mid-flight technical challenges, and consistently delivers high-value technical consulting. The impact you will have is substantial; you will help shape our technical services strategy and ensure all customers can cohesively integrate Ashby into their complex HR tech stacks.




YOU WILL ACHIEVE THIS BY:

 - Building and scaling a high-performing team, supporting both specialized Integration Consultants and Technical Solution Consultants; empowering them to comfortably manage high-volume portfolios while maintaining Ashby's high standards for quality.

 - Building the operational infrastructure required to scale technical services, including capacity planning, project prioritization, quality standards, and repeatable delivery processes. You know when to standardize, when to customize, and how to balance speed, quality, and customer outcomes.

 - Acting as a senior escalation point, leveraging your foundational knowledge of Workday architecture and complex API capabilities to guide your team. Diving into active integrations, troubleshooting roadblocks, and translating ambiguity into clear technical paths, helping your team scope solutions.

 - Owning the evolution of our technical services offerings, identifying recurring customer needs, evaluating opportunities to standardize solutions, and determining where new technical capabilities will deliver the greatest customer and business impact.

 - Partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Implementation to distinguish product gaps from services opportunities, establish clear ownership of complex technical challenges, and ensure customer commitments are both technically feasible and commercially sound.

As you're probably gathering, we're looking for someone who has been in the trenches, led high-volume functions, and built and scaled a team of technical consultants. You've done this work yourself, and you bring real "I've been there" credibility and empathy for customers navigating complex tools.



To be qualified for this role, you must have the following:

 - 8+ years of experience in technical consulting, integration services, or technical implementations, with at least 3+ years directly managing and scaling a team of technical resources.

 - Strong working knowledge of enterprise integrations, including Workday architecture, APIs, authentication, data mapping, and integration design.  - Brainstorm and validate solutions to complex integration hurdles when your team gets stuck.

 - Scope mid-flight pivots; when a customer suddenly requires a custom build instead of a standard integration, you must be able to step in and define that technical path.
